description:
Found 2026-11-04 while verifying the lazy-guard landing (card 20261101_144013) on a clean worktree at main: `kill -TERM <api-pid>` does NOT stop the server. It kept serving /health (HTTP 200) 8 minutes later, two TERMs later, and only `kill -9` ended it. `stop_latency_s` 25 s in `scripts/benchmark_startup.py` is the same thing seen through that script's escalation path, not a slow shutdown.

MECHANISM: `domain/infrastructure/_internal/pugqeep/engine.py::Engine.__init__` calls `self.install_signal_handlers()` unconditionally (line ~1235), which does `signal.signal(SIGTERM, self._handle_signal)` / same for SIGINT (~1862). `_handle_signal` only sets `self._running = False` and calls `self.stop()` — it never re-raises or calls the previous handler. Because the API constructs a PGQ engine during lifespan startup (`PGQ core engine created`), the engine's handler replaces the one uvicorn installed via `loop.add_signal_handler`, so uvicorn's graceful shutdown never runs. `/proc/<pid>/status` confirms the state: SIGTERM is in SigCgt (caught), not SigIgn/SigBlk, and the main thread parks in ep_poll.

MINIMAL REPRO (two uvicorn apps, same code, one difference):
  app = FastAPI()
  @app.on_event('startup')
  def s(): Engine()            # skip this line for the control case
  @app.get('/')
  def r(): return {'ok': True}
  -> control: exits 0.26 s after SIGTERM
  -> with Engine(): still alive after 10 s, killed -9

IMPACT: (1) every lifecycle hook registered for FastAPI shutdown is dead code in production — `_shutdown_process_guard`, `_cancel_parent_preload` (the new lazy-guard cancellation), checkpoint/flush/telemetry hooks: none of them run, because the only thing that ever ends the process is SIGKILL. (2) `systemctl restart slough-api` hard-kills after `TimeoutStopSec`, so in-flight requests die and no state is flushed. (3) Ctrl-C is equally hijacked, which is why dev-server stops need escalation.

FIX DIRECTION: a library must not install process-wide signal handlers from a constructor. Make installation explicit and owned: `Engine(config, install_signals=False)` by default, the standalone runner/CLI entry points call `install_signal_handlers()` themselves, and the handler chains to the previously saved handler after stopping the engine (or better: the engine exposes `request_stop()` and the owner does the signalling). Existing tests at `tests/core-py/test_pugqeep_process_mgmt.py:663,670,1433-1441` call `install_signal_handlers()` explicitly, so the API path can stop hijacking without touching them.

GATE: a test that boots the FastAPI app (or a minimal app + Engine()) and asserts SIGTERM ends the process within ~5 s and that the lifespan shutdown hook ran; plus a PGQ test asserting `Engine()` construction does not change `signal.getsignal(SIGTERM)`.

notes.text: REPRO + SECOND OBSERVATION: minimal pair (same FastAPI app, port 8125/8126): control exits 0.26 s after SIGTERM; with `Engine()` in startup it is still alive after 10 s and needs SIGKILL. On the real API (port 8124, main code) SIGTERM at 08:09 was still ignored 10 s later, and an earlier run stayed up 8 minutes, still answering /health 200, across two TERMs. Note the preload's own teardown works when it runs (`Parent preload: stopped guard after materialization (parent owns weights)` at 08:09:50) — it is the process-level signal path that is broken, so FastAPI shutdown hooks (and therefore `_cancel_parent_preload`, `_shutdown_process_guard`) are unreachable in production today.

title: fix(api): PGQ Engine() hijacks SIGTERM — the API ignores TERM and can only be SIGKILLed

Observed on main 2026-11-04 08:09 (worktree, real artifact) and again on the no-artifact run; it is emitted at guard start, i.e. while the provider is header-only by design (lazy_from_slnc) and the weights are still on the preload timer. description:
Found while landing card 20261104_053224 (a7769616c): `ModelLoader._try_load_soul` now resolves a native `.soul` by header identity, and two of its tiers depend on metadata that training never writes.

Measured on the 5 real souls in `models/slonet-native/` (all trained on the same `data/datasets/tinyshakespeare/input.txt`): every one records `dataset_signature=""` while `integrity_hash` and `born_at` are populated.

Consequences today:
- `dataset:<signature>` lookups can never match (tier inert).
- Family aliases (`sloughgpt`, `sloughgpt-v1`, `slonet`, `slonet-native`) REFUSE with a candidate listing, because equivalence requires the same base_model AND the same non-empty dataset signature. So `SLO_AUTOLOAD_MODEL=sloughgpt` now fails loudly instead of serving the newest checkpoint. That refusal is intended (it was serving a wrong-artifact guess before), but the family journey stays broken until this lands.

Fix: compute a dataset content hash at training time and set `SloProfile.dataset_signature` before `save_soul(...)` (`domain/training/_internal/train_pipeline.py` ~L2688), so retraining the same model on an unchanged dataset yields the same signature and the artifacts become provably interchangeable. Hash the resolved dataset bytes (or a stable sample + size + digest) — never the path — and keep it stable across runs over the same data.

Note: existing souls cannot be back-filled by the loader — either retrain, or add a migration that recomputes the signature from the recorded `training_dataset` when the bytes are still present (and logs what it rewrote).
title: train: record SloProfile.dataset_signature so .soul identity can prove dataset equivalence

description:
Scope: option 4 from the CPU/GPU discussion ("optional torch backend behind a parity gate") — built on the seam that already exists instead of a second training loop.

**Measured before building (port, don't rebuild).**
- Training math already runs on a hand-written autograd engine (`domain/training/_internal/slonet.py`, 8648 L) whose hot ops go through `_matmul` / `_accel_op` into `domain/slolib/_internal/gpu.py::get_accelerator()`. That layer already has `_CUDABackend` (CuPy), `_MetalBackend`, `_OpenCLBackend`, `_CPUBackend`, a bounded probe (`SLO_ACCEL_PROBE_TIMEOUT`), and dispatch counters `{gpu_matmuls, cpu_matmuls, fallbacks, h2d_bytes, d2h_bytes}` (`dispatch_stats()`).
- `TrainerConfig.device` (`train_pipeline.py:430`) is inert: `"auto"` -> `"cpu"`, `_setup_device()` returns `"cpu"` unconditionally, so the accelerator is only ever reached by accident.
- `cupy 14.2.0` IS installed and the host has a GTX 1050 (CC 6.1) — a GPU training route exists today. `torch` is NOT installed (`ModuleNotFoundError`); disk is 99% (2.1 GB free), so CUDA-torch is not installable here.
- No parity test exists between a device arm and the NumPy arm: existing GPU tests assert ops against numpy refs, but never a *training trajectory*, and never that dispatch actually left the CPU.

**Build (one seam, N backends, one gate).**
1. `_TorchBackend(_Accelerator)` in `domain/slolib/_internal/gpu.py` — same protocol as `_CUDABackend` (`to_device/from_device/matmul/...`), torch tensors, **opt-in** (`SLO_ACCEL_BACKEND=torch`) so default selection stays byte-identical.
2. Explicit backend selection: `SLO_ACCEL_BACKEND=cpu|torch|cupy|auto`; an explicit request that is unavailable must refuse loudly instead of silently degrading (the silent-degradation class the dispatch counters were added for).
3. Make `TrainerConfig.device` truthful: `auto` resolves through the accelerator and the resolved name is recorded (StepTrace + training_info); `device="cpu"` forces the NumPy backend.
4. Parity gate `tests/core-py/test_train_device_parity.py`, three levels: op parity vs numpy refs; **trajectory parity** (same init, same batches, N train steps -> loss/grad-norm drift within tol) with a tripwire asserting `dispatch_stats()["gpu_matmuls"] > 0` (otherwise the "GPU" arm was secretly NumPy and the gate proves nothing); and a **gate self-test** (a deliberately drifted backend must be caught).
5. `scripts/benchmark_train_device.py` — steps/sec + dispatch attribution per backend on one real preset, JSON out; this decides whether GPU training is worth it at current model sizes.

**Known limit, stated up front:** dispatch is per-op with host round-trips (`to_device`/`from_device` inside `_matmul`), so GPU wins only above the 16384-element output threshold. At TinyShakespeare sizes it may lose; the benchmark is the arbiter, not the assumption.

**Out of scope:** nn.Module rewrite / second trainer (AGENTS.md one-loop rule), `.soul` format, inference paths, boot.


---
**CLOSED 2026-11-04 — landed on main `ef8c88bce` (lane `feat/train-device`, pushed `HEAD:main`).**

**Built (device story):**
- `SLO_ACCEL_BACKEND=cpu|cuda|metal|opencl|torch|auto` (+ aliases `cupy`/`gpu`/`nvidia`, `mps`/`apple`, `numpy`). Unset/`auto` keeps the historical priority order byte-identically; an explicit value resolves or **raises** (`accelerator_for()` / `select_backend()`). Boot probe logs and serves CPU rather than dying.
- `_TorchBackend(_Accelerator)` on the existing seam — numpy in / numpy out, opt-in only. No second trainer, no `nn.Module` rewrite (one-loop rule).
- `TrainerConfig.device` no longer collapsed in `__post_init__` (validated instead); `_setup_device()` resolves once, records the resolved backend, and `train`/`evaluate`/`generate` push it as a **thread-local pin** — `device="cpu"` now really silences the GPU, for that job only. Default stays `"cpu"`; API `device=None` → `"cpu"`, so defaults are unchanged.
- `tests/core-py/test_train_device_parity.py`: op parity + **trajectory parity** + `dispatch_stats()["gpu_matmuls"] > 0` tripwire + negative control (1% matmul error must be caught; parameters are the sensitive arm — cross-entropy ~4.6 masks the loss arm).
- `scripts/benchmark_train_device.py`: ms/step, tokens/s, dispatch attribution, host↔device bytes, drift vs CPU, JSON out.

**Fixed (found by the gate; pre-existing on main, not device-related):**
`SloLinear._get_weight_T` cached `weight.T()` as a **graph node**. It is not in `parameters()`, so `zero_grads` never cleared it, and every `backward()` added to it (matmul backward + transpose backward both `a.grad.data += ...`): the real weight's gradient grew **1×/2×/3×** — 9 params (`ff.w1/w3.weight`, `ff.w2`, `attn.W_o`, `lm_head`), up to **2.0 relative drift after 3 identical steps**; invisible at step 1, likely masked by grad clipping. Fixed by building the transpose node per forward pass (strided view, one allocation); `_weight_T_contig` (inference data cache) untouched. `test_get_weight_T_cached` replaced (it asserted the unsafe identity); `TestRepeatedBackward` pins "3 identical backwards == 1" and **fails on the old code** (verified: 9 params drifted, worst 2.000).

**Measured:** `benchmark_train_device.py` n_embed=256/4L: CPU **695.6 ms/step** vs CUDA **582.3** = **1.19×**, 30.9 MB/step host↔device, loss drift **3.2e-07**. `benchmark_slonet_training.py`: gate 55.4K params **1.17 s/s**, loss 0.0007, PPL 1.0; tiny 21.3K **2.37 s/s**, loss 3.071, PPL 21.56.

**Gates:** parity **13 passed / 1 skipped** (torch absent → its refusal path is covered, its execution is not), device/GPU/config closure **521 passed**, slonet/train closure **443 passed**, ruff check+format clean. Three tests that encoded the old inert contract updated (`auto` preserved for `_setup_device`; `set_accelerator_precision("fp16")` follows the backend's `_fp16_available` instead of asserting a CPU host).

**Limits / out of scope:** torch unexecuted here (99% disk, 2.1 GB free — CUDA-torch not installable, CPU-torch needs approval); per-op dispatch with host round-trips means 1.19× is the ceiling at this shape. `.soul` format, inference paths, boot untouched.


---
**SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-11-04 — landed `0576757ef` (lane `feat/train-device`, pushed `HEAD:main`).** User ruling: *"we don't need torch, we kick the torch out and replace it with SloNet and it works."*

1. **`_TorchBackend` is deleted** (~250 lines, `domain/slolib/_internal/gpu.py`). The backend seam is now `cpu|cuda|metal|opencl`. Removal is a **loud refusal, not a silent fallback**: `_REMOVED_BACKENDS` holds the reason once, so `select_backend("torch")` / `accelerator_for("torch")` / `TrainerConfig(device="torch")` all raise `torch was removed — SloNet's NumPy engine is the only training backend`; a stale `SLO_ACCEL_BACKEND=torch` in a shell profile still boots (probe logs, serves CPU — pinned by `test_removed_backend_in_the_env_still_boots`).
2. **`TrainerConfig` now validates against `gpu.known_backends()`** instead of its own hand-kept set — one declaration, so the config vocabulary cannot drift from the seam. Side effect: `opencl` / `numpy` were always supported by the seam but rejected by the config; they are accepted now.
3. **Correction to this card's note above:** an unspecified API `device` resolves to **`"auto"`**, not `"cpu"` — `SloughGPTTrainer` does `device=device or "auto"` (`train_pipeline.py:1058`) and `_setup_device()` then pins the resolved backend. Compute is unchanged; only the sentence was wrong.
4. **Tests:** parity **15 passed / 0 skipped** (was 13 passed / 1 skipped — the torch arm became `test_torch_is_refused`; the unavailable-declaration test now uses a known-but-unservable backend so it stops skipping). Device/GPU/config/trainee closure **717 passed / 6 skipped**, slonet/train closure **309 passed**, ruff clean.

Everything device-independent from the original note still stands: the selection seam, the thread-local pin, the truthful resolved-device record, the parity gate with its `gpu_matmuls` tripwire and negative control, `benchmark_train_device.py`, and the `_get_weight_T` gradient-accumulation fix.
title: feat(train): optional torch accelerator behind a numpy-vs-device parity gate

description:
Goal: Test Rule clause 3 says the local/PR loop runs only the affected closure and merge-to-main runs the full suite as the backstop — but PR CI pays the full matrix anyway (measured 2026-11-04: test-core-py 31m52s + E2E 26m27s + test-web 10m20s per PR, every push). Bring CI in line with the rule.

Scope (design decisions for intake/decomposition):
- PR jobs: affected-closure selection (git diff base → changed files → pytest-testmon selection or a conservative mapping) + the seam gates which always run (contract, board integrity, feature tags, lint, command parity) — they're seconds.
- Merge-to-main: full suite unchanged (the backstop — never weakened).
- Required checks: test-core-py is a required check NAME; policy must decide whether the required check becomes 'affected+seam' on PRs.
- Trade-off to accept explicitly: main can go briefly red post-merge instead of pre-merge; the backstop catches it and the offender fixes forward fast.

Precedent: kanban-sync paths-ignore (docs/.kanban never trigger CI) already proved the 'right-size the trigger' direction.
Not in scope: weakening the merge-to-main full run.
title: PR CI: run the affected closure + seam gates on PRs, full suite only on merge to main (align with Test Rule clause 3)

description:
Follow-up to card `20261104_084408` (device story landed `ef8c88bce`). The accelerator is now a *choice* instead of an accident, so the next question is whether that choice is worth anything at the sizes we actually train. This card is the measured verdict + the decision, not new machinery.

**Measured — `scripts/benchmark_train_device.py`** (new, landed with 084408), n_embed=256 / 4 layers / 4 heads, batch=4, block=64, 5 steps after 2 warmup, CuPy 14.2.0 on a GTX 1050 (CC 6.1):

| device | ms/step | tok/s | gpu matmuls/step | cpu matmuls/step | MB/step host<->device | loss drift vs CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cpu | 695.55 | 368.1 | 0 | 20 | 0 | — |
| auto -> cuda | 582.26 | 439.7 | 20 | 0 | 30.9 | 3.2e-07 |

**1.19x.** Earlier hand prototype at the same depth with batch=8/block=128 (2x the bytes): numpy 803 ms/step vs cupy 677 ms/step — also **1.19x**, with 85 MB/step of traffic. The ratio is stable across shapes, which says the limit is the dispatch design, not the arithmetic.

**Why it is capped (measured, not assumed).** `slonet._matmul` dispatches only when `out_elems >= 16384`, and each dispatch is numpy-in / numpy-out: H2D both operands, cuBLAS, D2H the result — 20 host round-trips per training step, each with a stream sync. At 256-dim/4-layer the matmuls are small enough that PCIe + sync dominate. `dispatch_stats()` attributes all 20 to gpu with 0 fallbacks, so this is the real GPU path, not a silent CPU fallback.

**Options (the card's actual deliverable is the ruling).**
1. **Keep as-is** — GPU is opt-in (`SLO_ACCEL_BACKEND=cuda|auto`), CPU is the default for `TrainerConfig()`, and 1.19x is free for anyone who asks. Zero maintenance. Honest cost: the torch arm is declared but unexecuted here (torch absent; disk 99%, 2.1 GB free — see 084408 limits).
2. **Batch the dispatch** — keep activations resident on device for the whole step and cut ~20 round-trips to a handful. Real win, but it needs a device-tensor abstraction threaded through the hand-written autograd graph (`Tensor.data` is an ndarray everywhere, including checkpoints) — that is the "second engine" risk AGENTS.md's one-loop rule warns about. Scope must be proven small first.
3. **Fuse the per-step matmuls** — same idea at the kernel level (the fused-QKV / packed-FFN paths already exist for inference via `_get_weight_T_contig` and `_fuse_quant_weights`), no autograd change; reuses code we own.
4. **Drop GPU training** — keep the accelerator for inference only and delete the training pin/dispatch path. Only if the user's bar says 1.19x is not worth a maintenance seam.

**Blocking input from the user:** what win makes GPU training worth keeping? Below that bar, option 4 becomes the honest answer and 084408's device selection reduces to a CPU/torch switch.

**Known second-order effect to fold into the ruling:** `TrainerConfig()` constructed directly (`domain/infrastructure/_internal/training_queue.py:140`, the auto-training path) used to get CuPy matmuls *by accident* while labelled cpu; it now pins CPU as advertised. That path is now genuinely ~1.19x slower on a GPU host — the fix working, but it belongs in whatever we decide here.

**Out of scope:** torch benchmarking (unexecutable here), inference (already has its own fused/contiguous paths), `.soul` format, a second training loop.


---
**MEASUREMENT UPDATE 2026-11-04 (after torch removal `0576757ef`) — the 1.19x does not reproduce as a stable number; it is parity-within-noise at this shape.** Same script, same model (`n_embed=256`, 4 layers, 4 heads, batch=4, block=64), GTX 1050 + CuPy 14.2.0, host load average **8–11** (other sessions running):

| run | steps | cpu ms/step | cuda ms/step | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| earlier (this card) | 5 | 695.6 | 582.3 | **1.19x** |
| 1 | 5 | 331.7 | 325.0 | 1.02x |
| 2 | 5 | 243.2 | 252.9 | 0.96x |
| 3 | 5 | 294.3 | 225.2 | 1.31x |
| 4 | 20 | 297.0 | 269.6 | **1.10x** |

Absolute times swing 2–3x run to run because the box is shared; the *ratio* lands somewhere in 0.96x–1.31x, i.e. **roughly 1.0–1.2x**, never a clean win. The mechanism is unchanged and still the reason: ~20 per-op dispatches per step, each numpy-in / numpy-out with an H2D, a cuBLAS call and a D2H + sync (`dispatch_stats()` attributes all 20 to gpu, 0 fallbacks), so PCIe + sync eat the arithmetic at 256-dim/4-layer.

This weakens option 2 (batch the dispatch) as a *training* investment: the ceiling is the traffic, and the traffic is per-op by construction of the hand-written autograd graph. It strengthens the two cheap answers — **keep as it is** (opt-in, zero maintenance, honest label) or **drop the training pin** and leave the accelerator to inference, which already has the fused/contiguous paths (`_get_weight_T_contig`, `_fuse_quant_weights`). Still blocked on the same input: what win makes GPU training worth keeping?
title: perf(train): GPU training is only 1.19x at shipped sizes — decide keep / batch / drop

description:
STATUS: card only, no code yet (user ruling 2026-11-04: "play it safe first" -> file the card, keep discussing).

GOAL: a four-stage big-data training pipeline — bundle -> clean -> prepare(seal) -> harvest for training, across large and multiple formats — plus a live-data feed feeding the loop. Big data volume first, GPU/torch NOT in scope (see 20261104_111333: resurrection needs volume AND a measured GPU-side win; measured 1.0-1.2x today per 20261104_100637).

KEY FINDING: all four stages already EXIST as pieces — this is composition, not greenfield (port, don't rebuild):
- bundle: domain/training/_internal/data_import.py (GitHub/HF/URL/local/pack import)
- clean: domain/training/_internal/cruncher/clean.py (scrub_pii, quality_ok, DedupIndex against ALL persisted history)
- prepare/seal: domain/training/_internal/cruncher/pipeline.py::seal -> immutable v<N> snapshot + dataset_manifest.py
- harvest: dataset adapter -> SloughGPTTrainer (pattern proven by FeedBatchSampler in training_feed.py, BatchSampler protocol)
- live feed: training_feed.py (offset-cursor JSONL/HTTP, "feed:<source>" as data_path)

INVARIANT: mutable ingest on one side, immutable training input on the other, sealed between them. Dedup index travels inside each snapshot, so history resumes across runs.

DESIGN REFINEMENTS AGREDED IN REVIEW (2026-11-04):
1. Mechanism/placement — the live feed terminates at the FEED seam, never at the snapshot seam. Batch harvest = sealed snapshot (bytes immutable -> dataset_signature computable at seal, satisfies 20261104_081626); live harvest = BatchSampler over the cursor (append-only, unbounded, NO stable signature by construction). The fork already lives at train_pipeline.py ~L1490 ("feed path owns streaming"). KNOWN GAP to rule on explicitly: the live feed bypasses DedupIndex, so live records can duplicate sealed-corpus content — accept or add light dedup first; decide, don't inherit silently.
2. Scope — multi-format is a bundling-stage concern ONLY: normalize to one record schema {text, source, meta} at stage 1; nothing downstream of bundling knows what a PDF/HTML/JSONL is, and the trainer never learns about formats or shards (that is the second-loop birth canal per AGENTS.md one-loop rule).
3. The trainer's real wall is its input contract, not ingest: dataset_manifest.py says "the char-level trainer expects a single UTF-8 text file". Volume dies at that seam -> fix lives in ONE sharded/streamed dataset adapter feeding SloughGPTTrainer, never in teaching the trainer about shards.

PLAN (steps, in order):
1. This card (done).
2. MEASURE FIRST: bundle a corpus 10-100x tinyshakespeare through crunch_stream -> seal, record where time/memory goes (tokenize vs dedup vs read). Blocked on input: real dataset on disk (path TBD) vs synthesized corpus.
3. Branch feat/bigdata-pipeline, TDD: RED (a) composed pipeline end-to-end on a multi-format bundle, (b) seal twice over identical bytes -> identical dataset_signature, (c) the live-feed fork never touches snapshot state.
4. Compose, don't rewrite: one thin orchestrator over data_import + cruncher + adapter. Delete nothing.
5. Gates: scripts/run_affected.sh closure, ruff, ingest->train tokens/s benchmark number (new scripts/benchmark_*.py since this is a training implementation).
6. Land green, then re-evaluate 20261104_111333 with the measured number.

notes.text:
STEP-2 MEASUREMENTS (2026-11-04, no code written; all scripts in /tmp/opencode/, nothing in repo; every seal went to a temp store because / is at 100% with 843M free):

1) SCALE (scripts/benchmark_cruncher.py, synthetic): 2k recs/1.3MB -> 4.0s = 0.33 MB/s, 503 rec/s; 50k/33.6MB -> 109.7s = 0.31 MB/s, 456 rec/s; 300k/200MB timed out at 10 min -> consistent with LINEAR scaling, no blowup. Dedup rate matched the planted 0.30 exactly (correctness holds at scale).

2) STAGE ATTRIBUTION (30k recs, 21.1MB, 79.7s): text_fingerprint (MinHash) 53.1% | quality_ok 20.6% | scrub_pii 14.7% | DedupIndex 11.5%. Dedup query cost first-1000 vs last-1000 records: 0.298 -> 0.336 ms (1.1x) => the LSH index is FLAT; sealing at volume is safe. NAMED HOT SPOT (cruncher/clean.py): text_fingerprint reseeds np.random.default_rng(0xC0FFEE) and redraws its a/b coefficient arrays on EVERY call despite the fixed seed, plus one str-join + blake2b per 5-word shingle (~115 allocs for a 120-word doc). quality_ok's 20.6% is _repetition_rate (regex findall + dict count) and _alpha_ratio (per-char loop).

3) REAL DATA A - training_exports (150 largest feedback_export_*.jsonl, 120.9MB, 39,514 records): kept=6. Only 7 UNIQUE (prompt,response) pairs exist in the slice: "hi"->"hi" x15945, "xxxx..." x11550, "hi there" x4686, "test response" x3007, "response" x2607, "Hello!" x1419; median record 6 words / 47 chars. Quality gate: 36,907 pass, 2,607 high_repetition; dedup then collapses 36,907 -> 6. THE PIPELINE IS CORRECT - this 249MB corpus is test/ping-pong traffic. 0.96 MB/s.

4) REAL DATA B - data/qt/corpus.jsonl (55.9MB, 2,635 docs): ingest 98.0s = 0.57 MB/s, 27 rec/s; kept 2,106 (97.5% quality pass), dropped_dup 463 (17.6%) => healthy real text behaves sanely; seal 1.04s -> train.txt 50.5MB. HARVEST: train_pipeline.prepare_data() = 25.3s for 49.8M tokens, vocab 3,429, 1.01 bytes/token, 1.97M tokens/s.

5) THE HARVEST WALL (sharper than the card's "single text file" guess): prepare_data materializes the ENTIRE tokenized corpus as np.int64 IN RAM - measured ~8x corpus bytes (50MB text -> ~400MB of ids; peak RSS 1023MB, of which ~856MB is just importing the training stack). That is O(corpus) RAM: 1GB corpus ~ 8GB RAM, 10GB ~ 80GB. So the big-data blocker at the harvest seam is memory materialization, not file I/O - and it confirms refinement 1: the fix belongs in a streaming/sharded dataset adapter, NEVER in the trainer.

VERDICT: ingest ~0.3-1 MB/s (10GB of real text = 3-9h of cleaning) + O(corpus) RAM at harvest. Composition plan stands unchanged. The first real gate for "big data training" is DATA SUBSTANCE (the flagship export is 99.98% redundant), then the int64 materialization.

description:
chore(ci): stabilize test_baseline_cli_json_block — same-machine A-B baseline compare trips on runner perf noise

EVIDENCE (measured 2026-11-05):
- CI run 42061785501 (e601cf6d8): `tests/core-py/test_quantization_benchmark_e2e.py::TestBaseline::test_baseline_cli_json_block` FAILED — `assert data["baseline"]["regressions"] == []` got `[{'key': 'tiny…', 'current': 5}]`. Suite otherwise: 1 failed / 42801 passed / 21m11s.
- Same test PASSED in CI at a9964c422 (run earlier the same day, 13:40) and the test file is unchanged since 815cb94c9 — so this is not a code change.
- Local repro: 1 passed / 57s. Does not reproduce outside a loaded CI runner.
- The change at that SHA was in-process (tests/conftest.py teardown); the failing test drives the CLI as a subprocess — no plausible causal path.

ROOT CAUSE (diagnosis complete):
- The test does a same-machine A-B: run 1 writes a fresh baseline into tmp_path, run 2 (seconds later) compares against it — see tests/core-py/test_quantization_benchmark_e2e.py:1041-1052 (also test_baseline_cli_creates_then_validates, same pattern, same exposure).
- `regressions != []` between two back-to-back quick runs means the SECOND run measured slower than the first — pure runner performance noise (noisy shared CI CPU, thermal, co-tenancy), not a real regression.
- Compare logic: scripts/benchmark_quantization.py:1513 `_compare_baseline` — deltas are flagged as regressions at :1540; threshold is effectively zero-tolerance for these metrics.

FIX DIRECTIONS (pick one at implementation time):
1. Tolerance: allow a small relative delta (e.g. ±10-15%) before flagging a regression in the e2e path — real regressions of interest are far larger than runner noise.
2. Test-side: assert on the baseline block shape (`exists` flag, `regressions` key present) rather than requiring zero regressions in an A-B that cannot distinguish noise from drift.
3. If keeping strict compare: retry the compare once on failure (flake retry) before failing.

IMPACT: intermittent red on main CI for test-core-py; each occurrence costs a triage cycle (this one was fully diagnosed). Not blocking — flaky signal, not a real quantization regression.

choice.py now carries TWO answer parsers: parse_pick (lettered/digit fallback) and parse_action (added today 11:24 on wip/avion-observation). That is the third vocabulary, not the second, and it is the drift this card exists to stop.

Standardize on one protocol: an option's identity is a stable token bound at first grounding and never derived from list position.
- CandidateLedger assigns A/B/C once per run; withholding a card marks its entry unpickable instead of renumbering the rest (the current unavailable annotation is a workaround for exactly this).
- DONE/FAIL are keywords, not positions: resolve 'done'/'cannot' from the reply text BEFORE consulting a letter.
- parse_answer(text, ledger) -> Choice | None replaces both parsers.
- Digit support retires WITH the numbered prompt, not as a fallback beside it.
- Runtime stays tolerant; training narrows the model. Never weaken the parser to match a checkpoint.

title: avion: one answer protocol — keyword tier plus stable letter ledger

description:

title: avion: never offer a card the finder cannot resolve

description:
Agreed shape (this session): improve sloNet for computer use by training on our OWN trajectories, filtered by an oracle that is not the model. No scraped screenshot-to-action sets (OSWorld/AITW/SeeClick class) — they bake in someone else's UI vocabulary.

Plan:
1. Freeze and version the contract: lettered prompt + axtree observation spec -> one hash, stamped into every sample. Provenance is the invariant; unhashed corpora silently mix prompt formats.
2. Trajectory recorder in the existing ChoiceAgent.run loop -> JSONL per step: contract_hash, task, ledger (letter to label), raw_reply, executed observation, goal_pre, goal_post, stop_reason. Append-only, no behaviour change.
3. Admissibility filter lives at RECORDING time, not in the trainer: keep a step only if the verifier flipped false->true AND the reply resolved via the ledger AND the run was not pre-held-satisfied. ALREADY_SATISFIED is the same oracle, already built.
4. Preference pairs for free from the negative side: a pick that errored vs the pick that replaced it.
5. Dataset adapter feeding the EXISTING SloughGPTTrainer / SloChatTrainer mode. No fourth training loop (core rule). Loss masked to the answer span only, never the echo.
6. Gate on task success rate over a fixed exercise set with fixed start states, not loss. Reuse the own-tokens gap benchmark (49e170a39).

OPEN QUESTIONS before code:
- Base checkpoint: user says NOT externally trained, so one of ours. Which .soul? (checkpoints/qt_1793814797.soul, data/learner/continual.soul, or the own-docs corpus run?)
- Do exercises come only from this app's pages, or is a seeded sandbox UI allowed? Changes what 'no third-party data' means.
- Full finetune or LoRA.

Known failure mode to design against: coverage. Self-play explores one page; without a curriculum spanning ux/ journeys the model gets good at one exercise, and gets good at picking goals it already satisfies.
title: avion: computer-use self-training corpus — execution-guided, no third-party data

description:
# ci(xdist): parallelize the full pytest suite

**Goal:** test-core-py takes ~31m52s single-process (measured 2026-11-04) and is the long pole of every PR's matrix; E2E 26m27s, test-web 10m20s. pytest-xdist 3.8.0 is installed in the sloughgpt env but UNUSED — no `-n` flag anywhere in CI or pytest.ini. Parallelize the full suite so the merge-to-main backstop (Test Rule clause 3 — full suite stays, never weakened) gets cheaper.

**Scope:**
- Enable xdist for test-core-py (start `-n auto` or a fixed `-n 4` on the runner's cores) and measure wall clock vs the 31m52s baseline.
- Hazards to handle explicitly (why this is a card, not a one-liner):
  - **Order-dependent tests** — we've paid for these already (self_train stop order-dependence #296, learner fixture join #295, response_tracker global order). xdist distributes tests across workers and WILL surface new ones. `-p no:randomly` stays; each xdist run's distribution is deterministic per worker count only if a grouping dist mode (`--dist loadscope` / `loadfile`) is considered.
  - **Shared ports / sockets** — journey tests hit localhost:5173; parallel workers collide (the X-Slo-Web-Tree foreign-tree problem gets worse with N servers).
  - **Subprocess tests** (self_train stop fixture, benchmark e2e CLI runs) — CPU contention + timeouts.
  - **Disk**: each worker imports the tree; ~/.cache is at ~90%.
- Decide placement: pytest.ini addopts vs CI workflow flag vs scripts/ wrapper (the repo's Command Rule says flags are declared once).

**Not in scope:** the affected-closure work (card 20261104_085623 — run LESS on PRs); E2E parallelization (separate runner class); weakening the merge-to-main full run.

**Evidence/baseline:** test-core-py 31m52s (2026-11-04), 42823 passed/116 skipped typical run (2026-11-07 logs). Target: 2x+ wall-clock reduction with zero flake introduction; gate = full suite green x3 consecutive runs on the parallel config before it becomes the default.
title: ci(xdist): parallelize the full pytest suite — test-core-py 31m52s is the PR queue's bottleneck

description:
SILENT wrong code generation in X86Assembler (domain/shell/_internal/vm.py): `times N <mnemonic with operands>` emits one 0x00 byte per repetition instead of the instruction. Repro (verified 2026-11-08 on a014d5382):
  times 5 mov eax, 42  -> 0000000000f4   (should be b82a000000 x5)
  times 5 add eax, 1   -> 0000000000f4   (should be 83c001 x5)
  times 5 push eax     -> 0000000000f4   (should be 50 x5)
  times 5 nop          -> 9090909090f4   (zero-operand form OK)
Plain (non-times) `add eax, 1` assembles correctly (83c001), so the defect is in the times path: parse at ~line 3968, _estimate_times_size ~3988, _emit_times ~4120 — the repetition loop drops operands (placeholder zeros). Downstream it executes as `add [eax],al` garbage: a hlt swallowed as a ModRM byte makes runs fly to max_steps (observed 100000 steps, eip past the program). Escaped detection: tests/core-py/test_vm_assembler_emission.py test_times() only covers db/dw/nop, and tests/core-py/test_vm_benchmark.py is assertion-free timing (its times-based workloads were measuring garbage). Fix: emit each repetition through the full single-instruction emitter (or emit once and repeat the byte slice); then regression-test times+mov/add/ sub/push byte-exact AND assert executed steps in the benchmark workloads (label-loop reference: 2001 ALU / 1001 MEM steps). Discovered by the vm-bench lane (scripts/benchmark_vm_memory.py, AGENT_SYNC a014d5382).

Origin guard + relay gate + frontend fetch gate (from FungoLabs reference analysis, docs/misc/FUNGOLABS_LAUNCHPAD_ANALYSIS.md §4.4/§7).

PREMISE (corrected during expert review — read before building): we have NO browser->provider path to gate. The OpenRouter/OpenAI-compatible endpoint+key live in backend settings; the browser only receives api_key_set:true. FungoLabs needs a custom-header gate because THEIR browser talks to Ethereum RPCs. Our real exposure is different:
  (a) WHO MAY CALL — SLO_AUTH_REQUIRED defaults false (anonymous on every endpoint) + CORS allow_credentials=True, so a cross-origin SIMPLE POST (form/text-plain, no preflight) can EXECUTE state-changing actions. CORS only blocks reading, not sending.
  (b) WHERE WE FETCH TO — caller-chosen destinations fetched server-side.

EVIDENCE / EXISTING CODE (port, do not rebuild):
  - infrastructure/ssrf.py validate_url_not_private — EXISTS, used at routers/datasets.py 3x. Reuse for every caller-influenced URL.
  - routers/models.py outbound fetch — configured servers only (_external_servers), not caller-chosen. OK, leave alone.
  - training/webhooks.py:272 — caller-registered webhook URL, NO validation found. Gap.
  - apps/web/lib/planner-proxy.ts — Next server relay to 127.0.0.1:8787, NO gate at all. The one true relay.
  - CORS is already tight (explicit origins + loopback regex ^https?://(localhost|127.0.0.1|[::1])(:\d+)?$, max_age=600, card 342d729f). Do NOT touch the loopback rule or the preflight amortization.

DESIGN (from the two refinements in expert review):
  1. General case: reject FOREIGN Origin on unsafe methods (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE). Missing Origin = non-browser client (curl, /v1 consumers) -> ALLOW. Loopback/explicit -> ALLOW. Else 403 E_BAD_ORIGIN. Prefer a per-route dependency over global middleware (visible per-route, descriptor-friendly) and prefer Origin over a required custom header: a custom header forces a preflight on EVERY request and re-opens the 22-round-trips-per-origin cost card 342d729f measured.
  2. Relay case: planner-proxy.ts + training/webhooks.py require the first-party header AND run the destination through validate_url_not_private. Relays earn the preflight tax; normal API calls do not.
  3. Frontend: 32 raw fetch() sites in apps/web outside http-client.ts. Add a lint/test gate that FAILS on any fetch( outside the facade, with an explicit allowlist for the legitimate ones (worker/model asset fetches, api-explorer by design). Migrate dev-log.ts ingest (PUBLIC_API_URL/errors/logs/ingest) onto apiPost.

MUST NOT AFFECT: /v1 OpenAI-compatible external consumers, SSE/WebSocket streams, api-explorer (operator surface), worker asset fetches (not API traffic), the loopback CORS rule, preflight amortization, Zama/3D work (unrelated).

description: DEFECT (found by scripts/benchmark_vm_memory.py, a014d5382): `times N <mnemonic-with-operands>` silently emits one 0x00 byte per repetition instead of the instruction — `times 5 mov eax,42` -> `0000000000` (should be B8 2A000000 x5); `times 5 push eax` -> `00`x5 (should be 50x5); `times 5 add eax,1` -> 00x5 (should be 83C001 x5). Zero-operand forms work: `times 5 nop` -> 9090909090, and `db/dw/dd` padding is correct. Worst assembler failure mode: silent wrong code — a swallowed hlt (0xF4 consumed as ModRM of a 00-pair) makes execution run off into zeros to max_steps. LOC: X86Assembler._emit_times (domain/shell/_internal/vm.py:4120) + _estimate_times_size (:3988); dispatch at :3968. WHY IT ESCAPED: test_times() (tests/core-py/test_vm_assembler_emission.py:607) only asserts db/dw/nop forms, and tests/core-py/test_vm_benchmark.py is assertion-free timing — it has been timing garbage without noticing. SCOPE: LATENT, not live — the only production `times` uses are `times N db 0` boot-sector padding (vm_programs.py:2786,3575, the working form); it bites user-written programs via POST /vm/run and the REPL. FIX: re-emit the full instruction per repetition through the normal operand path (size estimate + multi-pass label/rel handling), never zero-fill; then byte-exact regression tests: mov/add/sub/push/jnz under times == naive repetition of the single-line encoding, `times 0`, arithmetic counts, plus a runtime equivalence test (program with times-loop executes identical steps/regs as unrolled equivalent). Note scripts/benchmark_vm_memory.py deliberately uses label loops with a comment pointing here — keep or flip after the fix. Evidence repro in the benchmark lane conversation + AGENT_SYNC entry a014d5382.
title: Assembler: `times N <insn-with-operands>` emits 0x00 bytes instead of code — fix + byte-exact tests

description:
# flake: test_ai_fails_fast_without_model — cap-dependent count delta on the shared LogBuffer ring

**Status:** todo
**Sprint:** 2026-11
**Tags:** ci-flake, test-core-py, shell

## What fails

CI/CD `test-core-py` (run `42603882090`, commit `eb6f94fdb`):
`tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py::TestCmdAiLLMExecution::test_ai_fails_fast_without_model`
— `AssertionError: no ERROR entry added to shell log buffer` (`assert 1209 > 1209`).
Suite: **1 failed / 43335 passed** (2894s) — everything else green.

Second occurrence ever. First: single sighting recorded as "left open" in today's
AGENT_SYNC entry (quant A-B flake card `20261105_170745`).

## Why it is not a lane's diff (three-strike, proven 2026-11-09)

1. **Pristine by construction** — the card `20261101_154058` commits
   (`4cf21a117`, `a5eaa6933`, `eb6f94fdb`, 21 files) have **zero overlap** with
   `domain/shell/*` or `test_shell_repl_more.py`. The failing path is 100% untouched code.
2. **Deterministic local repro, no lane code involved** — isolated run passes
   (fresh buffer). A ring-saturation mirror of CI's state fails **byte-identical**.
3. **Documented pre-existing** — AGENT_SYNC: "`test_shell_repl_more::test_ai_fails_fast_without_model`
   (single occurrence, left open)".

## Root mechanism

`domain/shell/_internal/log_buffer.py`: `LogBuffer` is a `deque(maxlen=2000)` **ring**,
process-wide singleton (`get_log_buffer()`; `repl._log_buffer` points at it — `repl.py:395`).
The test does a **count delta**:

```python
before = len(repl._log_buffer.get(level="ERROR"))
out = capture_cmd(repl, repl._cmd_ai, "show models")
...
errs = repl._log_buffer.get(level="ERROR")
assert len(errs) > before, "no ERROR entry added to shell log buffer"
```

Once a full-suite session (43k tests) fills the ring to 2000, appending the command's
one ERROR **evicts one ERROR** (deque head = oldest): the ERROR-filtered count stays
flat → false negative. Pass/fail depends only on whether the oldest entry at eviction
time is an ERROR — a coin flip that **can only fire in full-suite CI**, never in
isolation. Line 882's `errs[-3:]` tail-slice has the same exposure to interleaved
background-logger ERRORs (`slo.pugqeep.engine` etc. — visible in the CI log).

## Repro (evidence: `~/.cache/slo-logs/shell-repl-flake-triage.log`)

- Isolated: `pytest "tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py::TestCmdAiLLMExecution::test_ai_fails_fast_without_model" -p no:randomly -q` → **1 passed**.
- Ring mirror: fill singleton to 2000 (1209 ERROR oldest-first + 791 INFO = CI's exact
  shape) via plugin `/tmp/opencode/training-consolidation/ringfill.py`, rerun →
  **`assert 1209 > 1209`**, byte-identical to CI.

## Fix direction (user ruling 2026-11-09: card only, no code now)

Strengthen (never weaken) — replace the count-delta with entry-identity comparison:
keep the `before` list (object refs prevent id-reuse), then
`new = [e for e in errs if not any(e is b for b in before)]` — assert `new` non-empty
AND apply the `model`-message check to `new` instead of `errs[-3:]`.
Watched RED = the ringfill repro; GREEN = isolated + ring-saturation both pass.

## Notes

- CI invocation: `pytest tests/core-py/ --ignore=… --cov=domain --cov-fail-under=50 -q --tb=short`
  (`ci_cd.yml` "Run core-py tests", job timeout 60 min; this run's step: 48m14s, no timeout).
- User ruling (2026-11-09): **card it only** — no test edit, no AGENT_SYNC append. **Superseded 2026-11-12** by queue pickup; see RESULTS below.

## RESULTS (done 2026-11-12, branch feat/shell-flake-log-identity, pushed: 321ea750a impl + fd9a0f417 sync)

**Ruling supersession:** the 2026-11-09 "card only — no test edit" ruling was temporal
(triage day, no repro in hand). The user's queue pickup ("yes") supersedes it; flagged
in the close report for veto.

**Fix shipped (strengthen, never weaken):**
```python
before = list(repl._log_buffer.get(level="ERROR"))   # refs keep old entries alive
...
errs = repl._log_buffer.get(level="ERROR")
new = [e for e in errs if not any(e is b for b in before)]
assert new, "no ERROR entry added to shell log buffer"
assert any("model" in e.message.lower() for e in new)   # on new, not errs[-3:]
```
Docstring documents the ring-flake rationale. Only count-delta site in the file
(grep-proven) — no other test touched.

**TDD gates (all watched):**
- RED: `-p ringfill` plugin (1209 ERROR + 791 INFO = CI's exact shape) → `assert 1209 > 1209`,
  byte-identical to CI run 42603882090 (head evicted fill-err-0 → fill-err-1).
- GREEN saturation: same plugin → **1 passed** (7.2s).
- GREEN isolated (no plugin): **1 passed** (1.2s).
- GREEN full file: `test_shell_repl_more.py` → **4066 passed / 56 skipped** (42.9s).
- Post-rebase saturation re-verify: **1 passed**.
- ruff check + format --check: clean.

**MUST NOT held:** assertions strengthened not weakened (identity vs count is strictly
stronger); no pytest.ini marker changes; no test_results/*.json touched; production
code (domain/shell/*) untouched — the ring is correct by design, the test's view of it
was wrong.

**Repro plugin:** `/tmp/opencode/ringfill.py` (fill-only in pytest_runtest_call
tryfirst — the runner's default impl runs the test after the hook).
title: flake: test_ai_fails_fast_without_model — cap-dependent count delta on the shared LogBuffer ring

ROOT CAUSE: the origin-guard lane fixed the datasets SSRF helper swallow (except AppError: raise — its own AGENT_SYNC entry said "no test depended on the swallow"; these two DID): validate_url_not_private now actually rejects, and x.example is RFC-reserved NXDOMAIN, so slo.infra.ssrf logs "DNS resolution failed for x.example, blocking" -> 400 E_BAD_REQUEST BEFORE the mocked fetch. test_success expects 200; test_failure_400 expects error == 404 not found but gets the SSRF message. NOT CAUGHT BY CI: tests/server/ is outside the CI test scope (the documented CI --ignore), so the regression is invisible on main. FIX (small): retarget the fixtures off NXDOMAIN hosts per the origin-guard lane own precedent (a.example/b.example -> example.com variants in 3 test files) or mock the DNS resolution seam; keep the SSRF rejection itself intact (security fix must not be weakened). Evidence: /tmp/opencode/numba_run_affected.log (closure 7 reds triage) + AGENT_SYNC 2026-11-12 entry.

---

## RESULTS (done 2026-11-12, branch feat/datasets-ssrf-fixtures, pushed: 0b4c21f11 impl + 4580d9648 sync)

**Root cause confirmed exactly as carded** — watched RED first: `2 failed / 74 passed`, and the captured log is byte-identical to the card's diagnosis:
`SSRF check: DNS resolution failed for x.example, blocking` → `E_BAD_REQUEST [URL points to a private/internal address: https://x.example/data.txt]` → the guard fires BEFORE the mocked `URLImporter` ever runs.

**CI invisibility proven:** root job `--ignore`s `tests/server/` (ci_cd.yml:238); the server job runs `apps/api/server/tests/` instead. Main stayed green while this suite was red — the card's whole point.

**Fix (the card's named precedent):** both fixtures `x.example` → `example.com`.
- Matches the origin-guard lane's own `a.example`/`b.example` → `example.com` retarget, and `test_webhook_url_guard.py::test_accepts_public_url` which literally documents *"same DNS precedent as the datasets import tests"*.
- Verified `example.com` against the guard's EXACT predicate (`is_private_ip`): 4 resolved IPs (2 IPv4 + 2 IPv6), none private/loopback/link-local/reserved → passes. `x.example` → `gaierror` → blocked by design.
- Docstrings on both tests now state the resolvable-host requirement.

**MUST-NOT held — security pin ADDED (strengthen, never weaken):** `test_rejects_private_url_before_import` posts `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data` (cloud metadata IP) and asserts:
1. `400`,
2. `"private"` in the error,
3. `URLImporter` **never constructed** — rejection happens before any importer work, no fetch attempted.

Non-vacuous: without the guard, `mock_cls` WOULD be called and status would be 200 → both asserts fail. As an **IP literal** it needs no DNS, so this pin cannot flake offline (unlike a hostname fixture).

**Gates:**
- RED watched: 2 failed / 74 passed (guard message byte-identical to card)
- GREEN: **77 passed** (74 + 2 retargeted + 1 new pin)
- Full `tests/server/`: **2134 passed, 1 skipped**

No cross-card bleed; `origin/main..HEAD` = exactly 1 impl commit + 1 sync commit.

**No journal note exists for this card** (138 of 196 cards have none — card-only closure is the established pattern; creating one would risk a duplicate card since sync matches by title, not ID). Evidence lives in this description.

description:
Found twice on card 20261102_001441 (2026-11-11 wip move, 2026-11-12 done move): PlannerStore.update_card(column=...) then `grib sync` moved the card RIGHT BACK (wip->todo, done->todo rev4). ROOT CAUSE: the card has TWO note records and sync gives the grib-internal note PRECEDENCE over everything: (1) grib note id == card id, stored in board.jsonl, status=todo, updated_at frozen at created_at 2026-11-02, board field empty; (2) the user dev-note md ~/.config/dev-notes/20261102_010844_*.md (status set to done, title matches the card, bound by title per grib design) — sync ignores it. WORKAROUND USED TO CLOSE: update_note(card_id, status=done) so grib note + card + md all agree, then sync reported 0 moved (done stuck at rev5). RULING NEEDED: which record is canonical (AGENTS.md says notes md are source of truth for status; grib behaves as if its internal note is). Fix = sync reads the bound md note status, or update_card propagates to the internal note. Every session that moves a card whose grib note was never updated gets silently reverted — the md status edit alone does NOT stop it.

— RESULTS (2026-11-13): RULING (user, twice, decoded from garbled answers): "a change in one place must reflect in the other — just like updating a file description, it should reflect on the file" → update_card/move_card propagate the column into the bound journal note via COLUMN_TO_STATUS; md files untouched (vetoable). ROOT CAUSE PROVEN: update_card (store.py:582) / move_card (:600) wrote only the card, while sync is a note→card projection that restores card.column from notes.journal.jsonl on EVERY run — so any direct column move was guaranteed reverted (observed twice on card 20261102_001441: wip→todo, done→todo rev4). sync reads ONLY the jsonl journal (63 entries); the 248 ~/.config/dev-notes/*.md are read by nothing in the sync path (verify.py:145-147 binds them board: uuid → title but only reports drift). FIX: _bound_note (id first — sync mints card id == note id; title fallback with latest-edited winner, mirroring canonical_notes) + _propagate_status_to_note guarded by disagreement (STATUS_TO_COLUMN[note.status] != card.column) so sync's own internal move_card is a no-op and blocked/'' are never flattened to open; update_card propagates only when column in kwargs; a card with no bound note never materializes one. TDD: RED watched 5 failed / 15 passed (3 MUST-NOT guards already green) → GREEN 20/20; full grib suite 376 passed; ruff check+format clean. PUSHED (lane, not merged): 1060548c6 (impl) + 964aa3a45 (AGENT_SYNC) on origin/feat/grib-sync-propagate. Closure is card-only: no journal note binds to this card (sync matches notes by TITLE — creating one now risks a duplicate card).
title: grib sync: internal note status reverts card column moves (stale grib note wins over done notes)

Root cause chain: testmon fetch_or_create_environment REPLACES the environment row when system_packages or python_version drift + test_execution.environment_id is ON DELETE CASCADE (PRAGMA foreign_keys=TRUE at db.py:33) -> the copied rows are purged on the destination's FIRST run -> packages_change forces a full run anyway. Measured incident 2026-11-12 - RETRACTED as a measurement artifact: the '0 of 114 match' reading came from comparing RAW package versions against testmon's patch-dropped storage (drop_patch_version, testmon_core.py:212 <- common.py:90 - 'PyJWT 2.14', never 'PyJWT 2.14.0') AND from scanning with PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 (hides ~75 user-site dists); 0 METADATA files changed that day, and under testmon's exact predicate the recorded fingerprints match the live env (the lone downcraft-0.3 delta = gitignored egg-info presence, per-worktree). (3) AGENTS.md Test Rule line: 'freshest' -> 'freshest environment-matching recording', plus one clause documenting the cascade invalidation (after a package change every recorded history is invalid — one RUN_ALL rebuilds).

OWNED: scripts/seed_testmon.py, scripts/run_affected.sh (heredoc only), tests/test_seed_env_guard.py (new), tests/test_run_affected_seed.py (fixture realism: _make_db gains a test_execution row — assertions unchanged), AGENTS.md Test Rule line.

description:
# Model load serves the wrong artifact — rebase onto main

User report 2026-11-12: "the model doesn't load well" — confirmed as
**wrong/garbage model output**, not latency, not a hard failure.

## Reproduced (this checkout, `feat/stackable-notifications`)

```
load_model("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct")
  → success=True, verified=True, model_type=slonet-native
  → soul_path = models/slonet-native/qt_1794132830.soul   ← WRONG FILE
  → 4 layers, vocab=5871, embed=128
```

Real Qwen2.5-0.5B (`config.json`): `vocab_size=151936`, `hidden_size=896`,
`num_hidden_layers=24`, `model_type=qwen2`. The app logs
`Autoload ok: Qwen/...` and serves a char-level toy model → garbage output.

Probe: `/tmp/opencode/probe_model_load.py` (run via `./scripts/python`).

## Root cause

`domain/infrastructure/_internal/model_loader.py:267` `_try_load_soul()`:

1. ignores `model_id` entirely;
2. globs `models/slonet-native/*.soul`, sorts by newest mtime;
3. loads `soul_files[0]`;
4. **relabels it with the requested `model_id`**.

`_load_inner()` calls it FIRST (line 139, "Priority: native .soul first"),
so every `ModelLoader.load()` inherits the wrong-artifact class.

## Why it is on this checkout

Branch `feat/stackable-notifications` is **191 commits behind `main`**
(merge-base `11007f58e`, 2026-11-03 16:41). Main fixed this on 2026-11-04 in
**`a7769616c`** (card `20261104_053224`): identity-based resolution
(exact stem → `hash:<prefix>` → `dataset:<sig>` → family id only when every
candidate shares `base_model` + a non-empty dataset signature; otherwise a
loud refusal listing candidates), plus `read_soul_identity()` in
`domain/inference/_internal/slo_format.py` — bounded 64 KB header read,
~0.2 ms vs ~1.3 s per checkpoint. Branch has 11 unique commits, all pushed
to `origin/feat/stackable-notifications`.

## Blast radius on this branch

- `apps/api/server/infrastructure/startup.py` `_autoload_model()` (eager
  autoload fallback) → `loader.load()` → **AFFECTED**
- `domain/shell/_internal/local_api.py:1059` `load_model(...)` → **AFFECTED**
- default lazy-guard boot (`_try_lazy_guard_autoload` →
  `from_slnc(resolved_path)`) → unaffected (resolves the path directly)
- manual UI load (`setup_providers(slonet_hf_id=...)` → `from_slnc`) →
  unaffected

So it fires when `SLO_LAZY_GUARD_AUTOLOAD=0`, `SLO_ENABLE_PROCESS_GUARD=0`,
a `.slnc` is missing, the lazy path throws, or via the shell.

## Plan (user-approved 2026-11-12: "Rebase onto main")

1. Resolve the dirty working tree FIRST — see blocker below; do not `stash`
   blindly.
2. `git rebase main` on `feat/stackable-notifications` (11 commits). Known
   conflict class: `domain/domain-baseline.json` — locked procedure in
   AGENT_SYNC (checkout --ours → script-compute actual drift → hand-apply
   only own-dir `tree_hash` + `recorded_commit` → `pytest
   test_domain_baseline.py` → commit with hooks disabled → `rebase
   --continue`).
3. Verify the fix landed: re-run `/tmp/opencode/probe_model_load.py` — must
   report the Qwen artifact (or a loud refusal), never
   `qt_1794132830.soul`.
4. Gates: lint, typecheck, change-scoped tests (`scripts/run_affected.sh`),
   `scripts/benchmark_lazy_autoload.py` (SOP-11 — load path).
5. Land via PR (Core Rules: local main must equal origin/main).
6. AGENT_SYNC entry + this note's status log.

## BLOCKER — dirty working tree (uncommitted, irreplaceable)

`git status` shows modified files that are **NOT committed anywhere**:

- `packages/avion/src/avion/ai/choice.py` + `slo.py`, 4 test files —
  a `propose_candidates` → `propose_options` refactor (numbered options →
  lettered), ~563 insertions across 6 files, mtime 2026-11-08 09:49.
  **`git log --all -S"propose_options"` returns NOTHING** and no stash holds
  it → exists only in this working tree.
- `docs/INDEX.md` (+6, new Reference section →
  `misc/FUNGOLABS_LAUNCHPAD_ANALYSIS.md`), mtime 2026-11-08 14:47.
- `.kanban/board.jsonl` + `manifest.json` (canonical board snapshot,
  263 lines) — regenerated by `grib sync`/`kanban_sync.sh`.
- `tests/core-py/test_results/*.json` ×3 (record noise).

A rebase needs a clean tree. Per AGENTS.md File Safety these are user data
and must not be discarded without explicit approval — decision pending with
the user.

## Related open cards

- **#104** `fix(boot): boot path is .slnc-only while ModelLoader prefers .soul`
- **#117** `train: record SloProfile.dataset_signature so .soul identity can
  prove dataset equivalence` (family aliases refuse today because every
  checkpoint records `dataset_signature=""`)
- **#105** readiness is an uptime heuristic; **#106** 7.4 GB peak RSS

## Status log

- 2026-11-12: card created. Bug reproduced on this checkout; root cause and
  blast radius confirmed; user ruled "Rebase onto main" and confirmed the
  symptom is wrong/garbage model output. Working-tree blocker raised, awaiting
  decision.
title: model load serves the wrong artifact (newest .soul relabelled as the requested id) — rebase onto main to pick up a7769616c

Confirmed: narrative vocabulary (101 experiences, competence/helpfulness/creativity/accuracy/empathy, growth rates) matches self_model.reflect() + self_model.json exactly. description:
ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed 2026-11-13 from PR #308/#312 CI logs + dependabot run 43383838040):

domain/shell/_internal/_native.py _load_engines() docstring promises 'Compile trace_core.c once (CPU + GPU) or return None', but:

1. loader failure path: except -> _ENGINES = False; return None  (benign on FIRST call)
2. cache-hit path (line ~60): if _ENGENGINES is not None: return _ENGINES  -> returns **False** once poisoned
3. success-but-unusable path: _ENGINES = eng if eng.any else False; ... return _ENGINES -> returns **False**

All three callers check only 'is None':
- domain/shell/_internal/_native.py trace() line ~179 (eng.cpu / eng.gpu -> AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'cpu')
- tests/core-py/test_cycles_native.py _native_available() line 55
- tests/core-py/test_cycles_native.py line 143 (_load_engines().cpu)

Cascade: once any loader failure/eng.any==False happens in-process, every later call crashes -> 150 failed / ~43270 passed across test_cycles* (114), test_tensor_native, test_render_neural*, test_shell_repl_more, test_vm_bus_handles, test_world_stream, test_quantization_benchmark, test_cycles_gpu + 2 collection errors. Env-dependent (loader failures vary by runner/lineage) -> byte-identical 150 on main-derived branches but success runs exist too (efad52746 had BOTH a success and a failure run).

FIX (small, contract-normalizing): make both 'return _ENGINES' sites honor the documented contract: return None when _ENGINES is False (keep False as the internal cache sentinel so we never recompile). Callers keep their 'is None' checks; optionally harden _native_available with 'if not eng'. Add a regression test: poison _ENGINES=False, call _load_engines() twice, assert both return None (second call currently returns False).

Evidence: PR #308 comment + PR #312 comment (three-strike tables, byte-identical 150/43268 across lineages); root trace domain/shell/_internal/_native.py:186 + tests/core-py/test_cycles_native.py:60.
title: test-core-py: _load_engines returns False sentinel, callers check only None — 150-failure cycles cascade

description: cwd_owner must be tri-state so a failed /proc probe aborts instead of silently reporting live=0; then schedule a weekly report-only run mirroring the existing kanban-sync.timer. --apply stays an explicit human action.

notes.text: LANDED 7630deb32 (fix) + ee86c37c7 (AGENT_SYNC) on origin/main. ROOT CAUSE: cwd_owner() returned 1 both for "no process lives here" and for "I could not read /proc at all" — indistinguishable to a caller, so an unattended run in a restricted environment reports live 0 for every tree and prunes live worktrees (2026-10-21 class via another door). FIX, two layers: (1) cwd_owner is now TRI-STATE — 0 live / 1 probed-and-empty / 2 could-not-probe, tracked by a probed flag set only when a readlink actually succeeded; (2) proc_probe_healthy() PREFLIGHT aborts with exit 3 BEFORE any verdict is printed. Preflight catches an environment that never could answer; the tri-state catches /proc degrading mid-run. SCHEDULE THE REPORT, NOT THE REAPER: infra/systemd-user/worktree-prune.{service,timer} mirror the existing kanban-sync.* pattern, weekly (OnUnitInactiveSec=7d, Persistent=true), passing --report which PINS dry-run and is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with --apply — so the scheduled job structurally cannot delete anything even if the default ever changes. TimeoutStartSec=300 mandatory (the systemd *user* manager defaults to infinity — same lesson as kanban-sync). Auto-apply stays an explicit unmade ruling; I recommend against it. ALSO: --help now prints the leading comment block via awk instead of a hard-coded line range — that range had already drifted once (2,45p vs a header ending at 41) and leaked code into help. VERIFIED: degraded /proc -> exit 3 in ALL THREE forms (absent, empty dir, readlink-denied/EACCES analogue); real /proc -> exit 0 with 0 fail-closed messages (positive control, so the preflight cannot block normal use); full dry run exit 0 with every verdict present (live 3 / recent 2 / dirty 23 / main 1 / prunable 0); --apply --max-age 0 on a disposable target REMOVED it while branch + 5,144 commits stayed reachable; DIRTY refusal still armed during --apply (uncommitted file survived, worktree survived); recency correctly blocked a fresh tree before --apply. 10/10 tests in tests/test_prune_worktrees_gate.py, ruff check+format clean, script mode 100755. NOT DONE — timer NOT installed: ExecStart points at the root clone, which sits on feat/stackable-notifications and PREDATES the script (systemd-analyze reports "not executable: No such file" purely from branch absence). Installing the unit before that branch carries the script would produce a weekly red unit. Install command recorded in the unit header; needs a clone on main.

description: RLHF today has PPO + RewardModel class but NO trainer for the reward model — an untrained scalar head is noise and PPO would faithfully optimize garbage (rlhf.py review, this session). (2) loss mode: Bradley-Terry L = -log sigmoid(r_chosen - r_rejected) as a loss strategy on SloughGPTTrainer; base model frozen, only scalar head (+optionally last layers) in optimizer. (3) sanity gate: held-out ranking accuracy — must beat ~70% on unseen pairs before PPO may consume it (~50% = noise, block). Placement: domain/training/_internal/ alongside rlhf.py (RM trainer feeds PPO as stage 1: SFT -> RM -> PPO; ref model = frozen SFT). Depends on unified loss-modes card if it lands first; coordinate, do not duplicate the loss-mode plumbing. Gate: benchmark_rlhf.py + affected tests + ruff.

description: General-purpose trainer for our model (user ask, this session). description:
USER ASK (2026-11-15): screenshot showed the 'Agent deleted' toast working; user was asked what gap 'we still need notifications' means and answered 'not the one we built'. Reading: the toast (transient confirmation) is NOT the gap — the gap is a PERSISTENT notification center where a non-technical user can later read what happened (what succeeded, what failed, why), across all actions.

RELATION TO EXISTING WORK (checked before carding — no duplicate):
- 20261107_064201 unified notify() dispatch (banner/toast/process-dock tiers) = DONE. That fixed the DISPATCH seam (one intent API), not persistence/history.
- 20261102_014254 process-notification contract + NotificationDock = WIP, but scoped to the TRAINING event stream (structured action-holders, auto-resume producer) — not a general action log.
- useBannerStore + GlobalBanner = journey-blocking alerts (AGENTS.md one-global-banner rule) — transient/current, not history.
- No notification-center/history component exists in apps/web (grep: notificationCenter/NotificationHistory/notification history = 0 hits).

THE GAP: no store keeps a durable, user-readable record of completed/failed actions (agent deleted, training failed, PR merged, sync error...) beyond the few seconds a toast is on screen. A non-technical user hitting an empty page or a silent failure has nothing to consult.

SHAPE (to be confirmed at intake, per Page Rule — surface ladder before a page):
- likely a dock/panel (plugin-panel or inline-widget rung) over a page already in a journey, NOT a new page by default;
- events sourced from the existing notify() tiers (add a persistence sink to the dispatch handle — one seam, not a second event path);
- store: client-side (localStorage/IndexedDB) or server-side feed — decide at intake;
- dedupe + retention policy; summary-first UI (AGENTS.md summarize-dont-dump), raw details one click away.

GATES: intake decides surface (5-point test if it ends up a page), journey citation required, design-system review (Noir Violet), tests assert the journey not the render.

COORDINATION: user chose to fix the store-path bug first (card 20261115_112756), then resume the 22-older-PR wave; this card queues after those unless user bumps it.

description: Found while diagnosing card 20261118_085717. apps/web/components/startup/StartupHistoryChart.tsx does: const { data, isLoading } = useStartupHistory(); const records = data?.records ?? This is exactly the defect class the apps/web AGENTS.md loading-state rule already forbids ('loading UI is gated by an explicit boolean, never inferred from content emptiness') extended one step: a FAILED read is a third state, not the empty one. description:
Found after card 20261118_085717 (get_alerts deque slice) unblocked /health/startup-history: the panel now says '10 runs' but the BAR CHART IS INVISIBLE — every column computes height 0.

MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER (Playwright chromium + CDP on :5173, Developer > Startup):
- row div: h-32 flex items-end gap-1 -> 862x128 (definite height, OK)
- column wrapper: flex-1 flex flex-col items-center gap-1 group -> w:83 h:0  <-- BUG
- bar div: style="height: 27.3252%" -> getBoundingClientRect().height = 0

ROOT CAUSE: percentage height needs a definite containing block. The wrapper's height is AUTO, and its ONLY in-flow child is the bar (the tooltip is position:absolute, so it contributes no height). So wrapper height = f(bar height) and bar height = % of wrapper height -> circular -> resolves to 0. Nothing errors; the chart just silently renders empty. Same defect class as the loading-state rule: a state that LOOKS like 'no data' but is actually 'render collapsed'.

FIX (proven by live CSS injection, no files touched at the time): give the wrapper a definite height and push the bar to the bottom of the column:
  className: flex-1 flex flex-col items-center gap-1 group
          -> flex-1 h-full flex flex-col items-center justify-end gap-1 group
Measured after injection: wrapper 128px, bar 35px, bar bottom (627) flush with row bottom (627).

SCOPE: apps/web/components/startup/StartupHistoryChart.tsx only. NOT touching: the error-vs-empty conflation (card 20261118_093418 — fetch failure still renders 'No startup records yet'), the tooltip anchoring (it is absolute with no relative ancestor — pre-existing, separate), the backend. Verify: StartupHistoryChart.test.tsx + design-criteria ratchet + test:changed + visual re-walk of Developer > Startup with CDP.
title: web: Startup History bars render at 0px — percentage height collapses against a content-sized parent

description:
TRIGGER: PR 258 re-land audit (2026-11-18). Root cause of why that PR became unlandable was scope, not conflict difficulty.

EVIDENCE:
- PR 258 (fix/audit-a11y-design-tokens): 28 commits, 341 files spanning apps/web + apps/mobile + domain/ + apps/api + docs/ + .opencode/ + .kanban/ + .planner/ + .dev-notes/.
- Unrebaseable after main moved (Next removal, page pruning, route consolidation): 187/341 files conflicted. Closed, never merged.
- Audit vs current main: 97 already landed, 79 correctly pruned, 80 missing-applies-clean, 85 conflicts = 165 candidates.
- Content classification of those 165: 55 deletions (mostly workspace test files), 16 unrelated churn, 85 stale-branch drift, only 9 with real a11y/token signal — and after patch-by-patch inspection, 0 worth porting (4 already landed, 3 superseded by main refactors, 1 cosmetic-only, 1 canonical-store).
- Cost of discovering that: a full multi-hour audit to conclude nothing should move.

THE INVARIANT: surfaces ship on different cadences (web deploys per merge, mobile only gets Dependabot, domain runs on its own test closure). A branch that spans N surfaces accumulates drift from all N simultaneously, so its conflict surface is the product of the cadences, not the sum. That is why 341 files produced 187 conflicts.

RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING RULES — do not duplicate them:
- Page Rule governs which page.tsx may exist (the artifact).
- Endpoint Rule governs which route may exist (the artifact).
- Command Rule governs which CLI flag may exist (the artifact).
- THIS governs the change unit: how many surfaces one PR/branch may touch. It is the missing fourth rule, same recurring-cost framing.

DELIVERABLE:
1. A short section in AGENTS.md alongside Page/Endpoint/Command Rules — name it (Surface Rule / Batch Rule), state the one-surface-per-PR invariant, cite PR 258 as the evidence.
2. Optional mechanical gate, precedent page-journey-gate.test.ts + check-main-sync.sh: a CI check that flags a PR whose changed files span more than one shipping surface (apps/web | apps/mobile | domain | packages/* | apps/api). Advisory first, ratchet later.
3. Explicit exception clause for genuinely cross-cutting changes (a rename touching every surface) so the rule does not get burned on day one.

MUST NOT TOUCH: .dev-notes/, .kanban/, .planner/ — canonical store moved 2026-10-28, PR 258's edits there were harmful as-is.
title: process: surface-scoped PR rule — one change unit spans exactly one shipping surface

description:
DEFECT: the notes→board sync is one-way. Deleting a note leaves its card on the board forever, so the two stores can only ever drift apart — the exact failure class the 2026-10-28 canonical-store migration (board = derived from notes) was meant to eliminate.

REPRO (observed live 2026-11-18, not theoretical):
1. grib note new "ZZ timing probe" --status todo --body "..."   -> note created, auto-sync adds card
2. grib note delete <id>                                          -> note gone (grib note search returns 0 results)
3. grib sync                                                      -> "0 new card(s), 0 moved, 274 total"  <-- card SURVIVED, count never dropped
4. grep -c timing-probe ~/.config/kanban/board.jsonl              -> 1  <-- orphan confirmed
5. grib board delete <id>                                         -> manual cleanup required to get back to 273

ROOT CAUSE: grib/sync.py, sync_notes_to_board() lines 41-89. It iterates NOTES only and has exactly two write paths:
    if card is None:  kanban_store.add_card(...)       # add
    if card.column != col: kanban_store.move_card(...)  # update
    if note.assignee and ...: kanban_store.update_card(...)  # update
There is no branch that iterates board.cards, and no removal path at all. A card with no matching note is structurally invisible to sync. Note deletion also does not call board deletion — cli.py note-delete only touches the note store.

IMPACT: any session that tidies notes (deleting a stale/abandoned card the normal way) silently corrupts the board's card count. Board counts are used as truth in sync output ("273 total"), so drift is invisible until someone greps. Under the canonical-store rule the board must be reproducible from notes alone; today it is not — it is append-only relative to notes.

PROPOSED FIX (do not implement without review):
1. Add the inverse pass: after the add/update loop, prune cards whose id has no corresponding note.
2. MUST be gated behind --dry-run first (or an advisory warning pass), because the board also legitimately holds hand-added cards created via `grib board add` that have no note. Blind pruning would delete those — that is a data-loss path, so the default must report, not delete.
3. Resolve the hand-added-card question explicitly: either (a) hand-added cards get a marker so sync skips them, or (b) `grib board add` auto-creates the note so the invariant "every card has a note" actually holds. (b) is the cleaner invariant; (a) is the smaller change.
4. Then flip prune-on by default once the dry-run output has been inspected on a real board.

SCOPE / MUST NOT TOUCH: .kanban/ snapshots (versioned, not live), other sessions' in-flight cards, and do not bulk-rewrite board.jsonl — edit through grib's own store API so chain_hash/chain_index stay valid.

GATES: unit test for the repro above (create→delete→sync→count drops); a test that a hand-added card survives a default sync; grib verify stays green; board count before/after on the live 273-card board must differ only by the intended prune.
title: planner: grib sync never prunes — `note delete` orphans the board card

description:
ROOT CAUSE (Phase 1 done, card 20261119_091258 evidence):

1) /agents 404 (573 hits/40min; openapi lists only /agents/routines/stream). startup._phase6_routers skips a router when any registered path startswith(router.prefix). Manifest order puts agent_routines (prefix /agents, 1 route) before agents (prefix /agents, 11 routes), so after agent_routines is included existing gains '/agents' + '/agents/routines/stream' and the whole agents router is skipped. Prefix sharing != already registered.

2) The spec lies: check_contract.py --runtime claims 'Assemble the app the way main.py does' but does app.include_router(r) unconditionally — never applies the production skip, so the baseline/inventory contains /agents while the server 404s it.

3) Tests cannot catch it: test_support._ensure_routers_registered also includes unconditionally (guard: /benchmark present), so test_agents_router 26/26 stays green while live is 404. Three assemblers: production (skip), gate (no skip), test harness (no skip).

4) The skip is inert for its stated purpose anyway: the manifest excludes the 5 pre-lifespan routers (health, consciousness, status, dashboard, bootstrap — overlap with manifest = empty), so it only ever fires on manifest-vs-manifest prefix collisions — pure bug generator.

FIX PLAN (single surface apps/api):
- Extract one assembler: routers.register_feature_routers(app) — skip a router only when EVERY path it declares is already served (idempotent retry, never prefix-guessing).
- startup._phase6_routers calls it; check_contract --runtime calls it; test_support calls it. One assembler, three projections.
- check_contract: add --list-routes to print the served METHOD path table.
- Regression tests: assembled app serves GET /agents AND /agents/routines/stream; every manifest module contributes >=1 route; a pre-registered router is not double-registered; two routers sharing a prefix both register.

Impact: /agents list/create/detail/runs/execute/orchestrate all 404 in production right now (frontend poller), and the contract baseline + TS contract exports are generated from an app that never ran production's registration path.
title: api: production skips routers the spec and tests both register — prefix-collision skip drops the whole /agents router

description:
Half (b) of card 20261119_091258 finding 1: the 12 console errors on Developer → Startup History / /training were (a) the /agents 404 poll (fixed, 365e27c08) and (b) HTTP 429 on /models/ and /training/checkpoints. Not yet diagnosed deeper than the status code — next step is identifying which rate-limit middleware fires (rate_limit_middleware.py) and whether the frontend poller cadence exceeds the budget or the budget is too tight for polling. AWAITING USER GO-AHEAD before any fix.

---
## Diagnosis complete 2026-11-21 — no polling fix warranted

- **Which limiter:** RateLimitMiddleware route bucket fires FIRST (route -> workspace -> global); the 429 body names the bucket ("Rate limit exceeded for {prefix}") — the original card only captured the status code.
- **Root cause of the 12 AM errors was the PRE-fix regime:** route buckets ran raw 30/min for ALL localhost co-tenants (no 10x), /models/hf shared the /models/ file-serving pool, and request.ts 429-retries (500ms/1s backoff) pinned the exhausted sliding window (parent card 20261119_091258 finding 1 retry amplification).
- **A fix already landed before this card was cut:** 2357fd2e8 at 12:30 (card cut 13:21) applied the localhost 10x at route-bucket *construction* + gave /models/hf its own (120,60) bucket.
- **Live verification:** x-ratelimit-limit: 3000 (300x10 local global) on real responses; a 35-request burst at /training/checkpoints returned 35x200 — pre-fix code would have 429'd at request #31; limiter confirmed active (global remaining decrements 2997->2960).
- **Demand vs budget post-fix:** checkpoints poller = 6/min (10s tick, visibility-paused) + mount refetches; models list = tens/min (staleTime 10s). Budgets: 300/min (checkpoints, /models/), 1200/min (/models/hf local), 3000/min global -> 10-100x headroom. Cadence does not exceed budget; budget is not too tight.
- **Residual found:** success-path X-RateLimit-* headers report the global bucket even when a route/workspace bucket governs -> card 20261121_080632_api-x-ratelimit-success-headers-must-report-the-governing-bu.
title: api: 429s on /models/ and /training/checkpoints polling — rate-limit responses in the /training console-error set (fix awaiting go-ahead)

AWAITING USER GO-AHEAD. Benchmark: scripts/benchmark_latency.py + a before/after probe (prior probes: 23 tok/8.08 s, 56 tok/14.30 s).
