description: Audit finding (read-only, no code yet): training's state layer is the only repo layer that fails the descriptor-projected vertical pattern. Progress runs once server-side but is STORED, never PUBLISHED — three root causes: (1) POST /training/start (apps/api/server/training/execution.py:108) spawns a raw thread; on_progress (:377) writes only into training_jobs[job_id], no SSE queue attached → frontend polls GET /training/jobs/{id} every 3s (useTrainingPolling.ts:84). (2) GET /training/stream (training/router.py:630) is start-and-stream, point-to-point into the requester's queue (sse_stream.py:91-92, training_queue.py:77); TrainingRuntime (runtime.py) has register/sync/restore but no subscriber/broadcast — a job started elsewhere is invisible to every connected client. (3) useLiveTraining.ts:127 filters stream==='training' + lowercase init|progress phases, but the backend only ever speaks stream='auto-train'/TRAIN|PAIRS (training_queue.py:163, task_queue.py:292); the init snapshot is emitted nowhere → hook is connected-but-dead. Five stores: training_jobs (execution.py:296), TrainingRuntime, _LOCAL_JOBS (local_api.py, curriculum jobs = zero push channels), _turbo_state (turbo_endpoints.py:186), engine state (engine.py:657). Pattern family to follow (already in repo): Form A delta-push + client accumulation (training_queue.py:163, rAF batching/lossHistory in useLiveTraining.ts), Form B server-clock snapshot + changed flag (live_stream.py, LIVE_STREAM_INTERVAL=2.0, consumed by LiveFeedStream.tsx — already pushed, zero polling), Form C shared-frame coalescing (dashboard.py:330-356), Form D generation counter (response_cache.py:58-76). Design: (i) elevate TrainingRuntime to the single job store — training_jobs/_LOCAL_JOBS/_turbo_state become grandfathered adapter views; (ii) store publishes on every mutation → /training/stream becomes subscribe-only fan-out; polls demote to fallback-only (useErrorStream/useLiveStatus precedent); (iii) one envelope contract pinned by a contract test — stream name + lowercase phases + missing init snapshot, shared by web+mobile (mobile.py:1693 speaks its own 'training' vocabulary); (iv) untouched: 3 executors behind the sync-core/async-host seam, in-trainer optimizer, all existing endpoints (Endpoint Rule clause 5). Scope: apps/api + apps/web = 2 shipping surfaces → 2 PRs (Surface Rule); subscribe-only stream is a new endpoint → discussed here first (Endpoint Rule clause 1), api PR first then web hook swap. Gap list driving it: detail fields (loss/global_step/eta/steps-per-sec) have no push channel though on_progress already computes them; job-detail 3s (useTrainingJob.ts:97), logs card, turbo 3s polls; curriculum jobs in _LOCAL_JOBS invisible to all push. Gates: contract test + scoped pytest closure; no benchmark (no training-loop change).
title: Training live state: job store as publisher, subscribe-only /training/stream (no per-second polling)

description:
Diagnosis finding from card 20261119_132133 (429 on polling): on SUCCESS responses RateLimitMiddleware.dispatch sets X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining from the GLOBAL limiter (max_requests x multiplier -> 300/3000) even when a route bucket (/models/hf = 1200 local, /models/ = 300 local, /training/checkpoints = 300 local) or the workspace bucket (300) is the binding quota. The header therefore misreports the ceiling the request is actually counted against: a route-bucket 429 carries route numbers while every 200 carries global numbers, so the X-RateLimit/Retry-After pair cannot be reconciled.

Fix: on success report the GOVERNING bucket = tightest (min-limit) among route -> workspace -> global, ties resolve to the earlier-checked tier; 429 responses already report their own tier and stay. Rationale: every request consumes 1 from each applicable bucket, so the smallest-limit bucket always empties first (window differences only matter on limit ties, where check order breaks them).

Scope: apps/api only. No frontend/SDK consumer of X-RateLimit-* exists (grep clean; only CORS expose_headers in main.py), so the semantics change is safe. TDD in apps/api/server/tests/test_rate_limit_middleware.py (new test class, header assertions).

---
## Landed 2026-11-21

- Branch `fix/ratelimit-governing-bucket-headers`, commit `97f682955` -> pushed `5682b444c..97f682955` HEAD:main; AGENT_SYNC entry `4a9f3699b`.
- TDD: 3 tests red first (route 120/119 expected vs 3000 reported; local route 1200 vs 3000; workspace 300 vs 3000) + unrouted-path fallback guard -> 10/10 green.
- dispatch now tracks gov_limit/gov_remaining across route -> workspace -> global tiers (min-limit wins, ties to earlier tier); 429 responses byte-unchanged.
- Gates: ruff, board chain, feature tags, router manifest, ts contracts, contract-static, surface-scope single surface (api), run_affected 627 passed/0 failed + slow phase EXIT=0, benchmark_latency exit 0 (no baseline exists - none created unasked).
- No consumer found for the old global-only semantics (grep X-RateLimit repo-wide: only CORS expose_headers) - safe change.
title: api: X-RateLimit-* success headers must report the governing bucket, not the global budget

description:
MEASURED 2026-11-21. The step-level path gate (ci.yml:99-136, card 20261112_062436) means E2E only runs when apps/web|packages|workflows changed; otherwise every step is skipped and the job reports success in ~13s. So main's 'E2E green' is overwhelmingly a SKIP, not a pass — the job has almost no real signal.

EVIDENCE (identical failure, main AND PR):
- main run 44908497278 (push, head 7d13d630f) E2E job: 13:22:02Z -> 14:07:17Z = 45m15s, conclusion=cancelled, dying at step 'Run npm run e2e:vite'.
- PR #373 run 44908881354 E2E job: 13:26:42Z -> 14:11:57Z = 45m15s, conclusion=cancelled, same step.

- ci.yml:94 timeout-minutes: 45; ci.yml:95-96 comment documents expected '~30m' -> only ~15m headroom.
- 22 specs in apps/web/cypress/e2e/.

CONCLUSION: pre-existing, NOT caused by any PR under test — reproduced on main itself 4 minutes before PR 373. Because there is NO branch protection on main (branches/main/protection -> 404), the cancelled check does not hard-block merge, but it means every web-touching PR shows UNSTABLE and nobody can get a truthful E2E verdict.

WHY IT IS A CARD NOT A WAIT (AGENTS.md Work Selection Rule): the first time a check blocks >20 min, queue the speed-up. This blocks at 45.

OPTIONS (pick one, do not do all):
(a) Parallelize: cypress parallelization across runners (needs a record key / cloud service) or shard specs across a matrix job.
(b) Raise timeout-minutes on frontend-e2e (cheap, treats the symptom; still ~30-45m per PR).
(c) Split the 22 specs: keep journey-critical ones in the gated job, move slow/visual ones (visual-headers, visual-interactions, layout-overflow, zz-hydration-diag) to a nightly or main-only job.
(d) Find whether ONE spec hangs (start-server-and-test waits on http://localhost:5173; if vite never reports ready it blocks until the job limit). Diagnose with per-spec durations before choosing.

NOT to be confused with: 20261112_062436 (done — added the path filter), 20261107_112103 (todo — xdist for test-core-py, Python not JS), 20261119_144623 (done — foreign tree binding :5173).

description:
Found 2026-11-21 while triaging PR #370/#371 test-core-py reds. THREE-STRIKE: not a flake, not mine — reproduces on pristine origin/main (e2c71edd6) with: pytest tests/core-py/test_dashboard_router.py 'tests/core-py/test_settings_router.py::TestTrainingPresets::test_apply_preset' -> 1 failed, 9 passed.

MECHANISM (exact):
1. tests/core-py/test_dashboard_router.py _mock() swaps sys.modules['domain.settings._internal.persistent'] for a MagicMock whose get_settings = MagicMock(return_value={'settings': True}).
2. If domain.settings (the package) has NOT been imported yet when the window opens (true in affected-closure runs — collection of this file alone does NOT import domain.settings; verified), the dashboard endpoint's 'from domain.settings import get_settings' (routers/dashboard.py:244) triggers the package's first import, whose __init__ does 'from domain.settings._internal.persistent import get_settings' -> binds the MOCK.
3. _cleanup() restores only the mocked module entry; domain.settings stays in sys.modules with get_settings permanently bound to the mock for the rest of the xdist worker.
4. Later test_apply_preset -> settings.py:668 'from domain.settings import get_settings' -> ps = {'settings': True} (plain dict) -> ps.update('training', **config) -> dict.update with the string 'training' as a positional -> 'dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 1; 2 is required' (C-level raise, hence no update() frame in the traceback).

WHY INTERMITTENT: full-suite runs import domain.settings via earlier test files before test_dashboard_router runs (alphabetical d < s), so the binding is real; the affected closure can select this file without any earlier importer, and xdist distributes per worker (failed on gw1 in run 44905654091 and gw0 in run 44808431227 — burned one CI cycle on PR #371 and one on PR #370). Same class explains test_health_services::test_services_all_ok failing in the same run (settings service probe hits the poisoned import).

FIX DIRECTION (implemented on this card's lane): in _mock(), before swapping sys.modules, ensure the target's parent package chain is already imported (__import__ of the parent) so parent __init__ bindings are created from the REAL module; the mock keeps serving direct child-module imports. _cleanup logic unchanged (restore-not-pop comment already documents the split-brain reasoning). Residual risk to note: any module that does module-scope 'from <mocked child> import x' and is FIRST imported inside the window still binds poisoned — grep shows none today.
title: tests: test_dashboard_router's _mock poisons domain.settings for the whole worker — first import during the mock window binds get_settings to a MagicMock returning a dict (test_apply_preset ValueError)

description:
FOUND 2026-11-22 by Gen during card 20261121_150816 (deploy truth-pass), independently confirmed.

DEFECT: .github/workflows/deploy-git-sync.yml:54
    if: $${ secrets.TS_AUTHKEY != '' && secrets.DEPLOY_HOST != '' && secrets.DEPLOY_SSH_KEY != '' }
This is a JOB-level if:. GitHub's jobs.<job_id>.if does NOT support the secrets context — actionlint: 'context secrets is not allowed here'. (Step-level :86 using secrets IS legal; only the job-level one is broken.)

EVIDENCE IT HAS NEVER WORKED:
- gh api .../actions/workflows/deploy-git-sync.yml/runs returns EXACTLY 2 runs ever, both 2026-10-27T06:10, both conclusion=failure, at 0s with zero jobs and no log.
- So the workflow never got past YAML validation.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW (ordering hazard):
PR #375 (fix/deploy-pipeline-truth) DELETES .github/workflows/cloudflare-pages.yml as 'dead and redundant — deploy-git-sync already deploys main'. That reasoning assumed deploy-git-sync works. It does not. If #375 lands before this card, the repo has NO working automated web-deploy path at all.

FIX OPTIONS (decide, do not all):
(a) Move the guard into the job (needs a dummy step) or drop it and let missing secrets fail loudly at the SSH step.
(b) Gate with vars instead of secrets where a presence check is enough (vars IS allowed in job-level if:).
(c) Restructure as: always-run build job + conditional deploy job keyed on a repository variable.

ALSO NOTE: deploy-git-sync.yml:86 step-level if is fine. Do not 'fix' it.

Blocked-by: none. Blocks: PR #375 merge ordering.
Related: 20261121_150816 (deploy truth-pass), 20261121_152656 (e2e 45m).

description:
EVIDENCE 2026-11-22 (measured on Qwen2.5-0.5B model.slnc): file stores BOTH model.lm_head.weight and model.embed_tokens.weight — byte-identical (np.array_equal True), 136,134,656 params each. 630M stored vs Qwen's real 494M = +136M = the tied head duplicated. Disk 2.35GB -> 1.85GB if honored; load RSS +0.64GB (0.5GB fp32 anon copy + 136MB int8 copy — from_slnc copies mmap -> model params, fp32 kept since free_quantized_originals=False; mmap itself released, so it is ANONYMOUS RAM not reclaimable page cache).

ROOT CAUSE: weight_loader.build_load_plan already ties lm_head->tok_emb BUT only when lm_head is ABSENT from the file (weight_loader.py:277 native path, :382 arch path: 'if lm_head.weight not in loaded_params and tok_emb.weight in loaded_params'). File has it -> tie never fires -> duplicate mapped + quantized + resident.

FIX (user directive: 'this should be fixed in compiler, tested and optimized'): SLNCCompiler.compile_from_dict drops lm_head when byte-identical to tok_emb. Detection by BYTE COMPARISON not config flag (a stale tie_word_embeddings config must never silently drop an untied head). Both naming conventions (model.lm_head/model.embed_tokens HF + lm_head/tok_emb native). Log + record tied_embeddings:true in config JSON (distinguish tied from lost).

SCOPE MUST-NOT: old files WITH lm_head keep loading via map path (byte-identical outcome); quantize walks MODEL params post-load (unaffected); grep get_weights_dict consumers + tensor-count assertions in test_slnc_*/test_weight_loader before editing.

ACCEPTANCE: TDD red-first (identical -> deduped, differing -> still written, loader round-trip logits identical via tie path); slnc test closure green; recompile this Qwen file -> load RSS/time measured before/after (expect -0.5GB file, -0.64GB RSS); ruff clean.

CONTEXT: parked alongside the int8-on-disk loader-redesign card (learn-from-llama.cpp thread); dedup is compatible with either direction.
title: slnc: compiler dedup — stop writing byte-identical tied lm_head (0.5 GB file / 0.64 GB load RSS wasted)

description:
USER THREAD 2026-11-22: 'not optional, build it well' + 'we haven't built our model loader yet — learn from how these big inference companies do it'.

CURRENT STATE: model.slnc stores pure fp32 (compiler quantize=False default, FLAG_QUANTIZED_INT8 unset on the shipped Qwen file). Load path: mmap -> COPY into anonymous model params (fp32 2.35GB) -> runtime quantize=True adds int8 copies (+0.63GB) while KEEPING fp32 originals (free_quantized_originals=False default) -> 3.47GB RSS for a 494M-param model that should fit in ~1.1GB. fp32 originals are genuine anonymous RAM (mmap released by release_mmap_pages=True), not reclaimable page cache.

TARGET (llama.cpp pattern): quantize AT SAVE. File carries int8 + per-tensor scale (machinery EXISTS: FLAG_QUANTIZED_INT8, code_to_dtype, compiler quantize='int8' path, parser dequant-on-read). Loader reads int8 directly -> no fp32 originals ever materialize -> ~1.1-1.5GB RSS, faster load (skip conversion), smaller file (~0.63GB + scales). CRC32 checksums: user says verification should be DEFAULT not optional (verify_checksums=False today).

DESIGN QUESTIONS: lossy-at-save changes weights vs today's lossless-fp32+lossy-at-load (bit-identical today after roundtrip? no — int8 either way, but WHEN it happens changes checkpoint semantics: training saves must stay fp32! So per-purpose files: train ckpt fp32, serving artifact int8). Scale of change: compiler write path + loader + quant cache (.quant.npz sidecar becomes redundant) + tests. Also dedup card (tied lm_head) lands first — independent but same file layout.

NOTES: paired with compiler dedup card; benchmark_prefill/card 20261102_001622 memory findings motivate it (4k prefill peak 7.65GB RSS on a 23GB box, 8k OOM-killed).
title: slnc loader redesign: store int8 on disk (FLAG_QUANTIZED_INT8 not optional) — learn from llama.cpp/vLLM

description:
Follow-up to card 20261121_142900 (grib ledger subcommand landed 65a966a25). User ruling 'es' 2026-11-22: wire the gate + fix the malformed entry.

WHAT
1. `grib ledger check --baseline <json>` — baseline = list of violation FINGERPRINTS (never line numbers: the doc is prepend-only, lines shift on every entry). fp = `order|{date}|{head[:80]}` / `{kind}|{msg[:100]}` (both stable unless an owner edits the entry — then review fires correctly).
   - fp in baseline + still occurring -> known, allowed (exit 0 only when ALL align).
   - violation NOT in baseline -> NEW -> exit 1 (catches bottom-appends / malformed headers).
   - baseline entry no longer occurring -> STALE -> exit 1, "delete this line" — STRICT SHRINK (page-baseline / command-parity-baseline precedent: fixing something without shrinking the baseline reddens).
   - no --baseline flag: unchanged behaviour (exit 1 on any violation) — existing 14 tests must stay green.
2. Fix docs/AGENT_SYNC.md line-308 entry (content-addressed, not line-number — other sessions prepend): `**2026-10-30 — OPENCODE (merge-all lane): ... #251 swiglu-AVX2 (external). Conflict resolutions: ...` never closes its header bold (800-char single line, the doc's ONLY never-closed bold). Insert `**` after `(external).` — summary-close convention, user-approved.
3. Baseline file `packages/grib/ledger_baseline.json` = the remaining 4 order inversions (backdated inserts) AFTER the fix, with a comment that the list may only shrink.
4. Wire into ci.yml `board-integrity` job (runs every PR, stdlib-only, self-locates packages/grib/src — same seam as check_board_chain): `PYTHONPATH=packages/grib/src python3 -m grib ledger check --baseline packages/grib/ledger_baseline.json`. grib has ZERO deps (pyproject dependencies=[]) so python3.11 runs it bare.

NOT in scope: re-dating/moving the 4 backdated entries (history rewrite, needs separate user ruling); the gate stays advisory-equivalent for them via baseline.

TDD: fingerprint stability across prepend + baseline CLI accept/new/stale paths red first (test_ledger.py).
Surface: packages/* (+ meta: ci.yml, docs/AGENT_SYNC.md travel companions).

description:
MEASURED 2026-11-23. The quarantine step added in 2b7723ff8 (ci.yml, "npm exec -- start-server-and-test vite ... excludeSpecPattern=**/chat-inference.cy.ts") never starts Cypress at all — wait-on times out after ~5m and the step fails, so every web-touching PR now reports a RED E2E job that executed ZERO specs. The 45m hang it was meant to work around is still latent (see card 20261123_073036).

EVIDENCE (two independent CI executions, identical signature):
- main run 45131480931 (the quarantine commit itself, gate open since ci.yml changed): E2E job failure 07:29:40 -> 07:35:32; step log job 137547762097 = 298 x "Missing field moduleType" vite 500s, then "Error: Timed out waiting for: http://localhost:5173" (wait-on); grep "Running:" = 0 -> cypress NEVER launched.
- PR #377 run 45139895826, job 137625704818: same 298 errors, same wait-on timeout at 10:25:28, 0 cypress starts. (PR #377 is red on E2E for this reason right now.)
- main runs after quarantine (45139877460, 45159486173) show "E2E success" only because the path gate skipped the job entirely (heads 483b27c43/62e5e10a5 touched no apps/web|packages|workflows) — main has NO green execution of the quarantine command, ever.

ROOT CAUSE (local probes in the e2e-chat-hang worktree, same lockfile):
- probe A: under "npm exec --", start-server-and-test child resolves bare "vite" to REPO ROOT node_modules/.bin/vite (lockfile version 7.3.6), not apps/web/node_modules/.bin/vite (8.3.1). Root vite cannot transform the apps/web vite-8 index.html -> every request 500s with "Missing field moduleType" from builtin:vite-react-refresh-wrapper -> wait-on never sees HTTP 200.
- "npm run e2e:vite" (the pre-quarantine command) never hit this: npm run prepends apps/web/node_modules/.bin to PATH, so vite 8.3.1 ran — CI runs before quarantine did start cypress (run 44908497278 executed spec 1/22 successfully).
- local repro of the exact quarantine command: exit 124, 54 moduleType errors in 60s, cypress never started.

VERIFIED FIX (one line, local faithful repro):
  npm exec -- start-server-and-test "./node_modules/.bin/vite" http://localhost:5173 "cypress run --config excludeSpecPattern=**/chat-inference.cy.ts"
- server phase: exit 0, 0 moduleType errors, HTTP 200.
- full run with --spec agents-page.cy.ts added: exit 0, "All specs passed!", 5 passing (02:31), 0 moduleType errors, exclusion present in command line.
- local runs used --port 5174 + baseUrl override only to avoid the live dev server on :5173; CI is clean so the plain 5173 form above applies.

ALSO SETTLES the open "never-resolving await" hypothesis on card 20261123_073036: the chat-inference hang is an infinite React render loop, not a stuck await. BootstrapContext.load() commits payload (setData, line 69) BEFORE validating payload.members (line 72); cypress mockApiFallback answers GET /bootstrap with {}; CommandPalette.tsx:66 destructures bootstrap.members inside a useEffect -> TypeError -> DigestBoundary.getDerivedStateFromError returns null for non-digest errors -> no state change -> React remounts -> loop forever (faithful.log: 9,741 destructure errors + 9,834 recreate-tree messages at steady ~24/s, 14.6 MB; known-good 11-20 run had 0). Bisect (worktree e2e-chat-hang): 666249b8b passes clean (exit 0, 0 errors) -> 7c065f4ba first-bad (exit 124, 1,457 errors) -> origin/main (exit 124, 9,741 errors).

NEXT: land the one-line ci.yml fix (unblocks web PRs, incl. #377), then the app-side fix on 20261123_073036 (guard CommandPalette against missing members, stop BootstrapContext committing unvalidated payloads, decide whether DigestBoundary should rethrow non-digest errors), then remove the QUARANTINE block and re-enable chat-inference.cy.ts.
title: ci(e2e): quarantine command resolves the REPO ROOT vite 7.3.6 — every web PR's E2E runs zero specs and fails

description:
Problem: dev frontend is two-origin (vite :5174 + uvicorn :8001) and BROKEN on vite 8.3.1 — user define keys do not apply in dev (controlled test: built-in NODE_ENV replaced, process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL raw), so lib/config.ts evaluates raw process.env in the browser (no process → ReferenceError at import) → http-client/store/chat-controller chain dead → chat unusable (vitest stays green because Node has process — test-env parity gap). The repo already ships the one-origin model for the SERVED site: build:vite sets an empty API base, main.py retired --web (gateway serves dist-vite as document root, MAN_STATIC_DIR), and apps/gateway routes by REQUEST KIND not path (wants_document: Accept text/html = navigation → SPA shell; */* / json / event-stream = data → byte-relay; method gate: writes never see the static layer). Doc comment names the collision: SPA and API share top-level names (/chat, /models, /training — 600+ root paths), so a prefix table would shadow one side.

Design (user-approved direction: one port for the machine — app server + backend runner; frontend never names a backend port):
1. lib/config.ts: PUBLIC_API_URL = '' (same-origin). All consumers are string-concat (chat/audio, error-reporter, api-explorer, sse-client) — relative URLs; no new URL(base) patterns exist (planner-proxy uses PLANNER_API_BASE, untouched).
2. NEW apps/web/vite/api-relay-plugin.ts — dev face of the gateway rule, streaming-safe (raw node:http pipe, no buffering, no total timeout — SSE must pass through), target SLO_API_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8000; this machine: 8001). Classification in order: Upgrade header/HMR -> vite; /@, /node_modules, /__vite -> vite; real file under root or publicDir (with .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.json/.css extension tries) -> vite; API_DOC_PATHS (/docs,/redoc,/openapi.json) -> relay (gateway parity); Accept: text/html -> vite (spa fallback); non-GET/HEAD -> relay; else -> relay (API reads: /info, SSE GETs, audio). Registered AFTER apiRoutesPlugin so /api/(planner|calendar) keeps its dev handlers (they next() out of scope before us).
3. run/docs: start commands carry SLO_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8001 on this machine.

Scope: surface apps/web only (no API/contract/TS-regen changes; mobile + sdk-ts carry own base — out). Foreign :8000/:5173 never touched; no process kills (graft rules stay). Open: vite-8 define root cause (only two define keys exist today); gateway-fronted dev HMR (ws) is a later question.

Verification (TDD red-first): config.test pins same-origin '' (red now); classifier unit tests (vite-owned vs relay cases incl. SSE Accept and api-doc parity); tsc + eslint changed files; same-origin walk — POST /chat through :5174 reaches API and streams SSE, GET /chat returns the SPA shell, chrome-devtools journey if available. Card close: note evidence -> board done -> grib sync -> sealed ledger entry (grib ledger entry --text).

description:
**Goal:** `domain/infrastructure/_internal/quantization.py:1198-1210` publishes `_nb_kv_built = True` BEFORE assigning `_nb_kv_kernels` (which starts life as `None`). Any concurrent caller passes the flag, gets `None`, and `quantize_kv_tensor` then does `qk, _ = _get_nb_kv_kernels()` -> `TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object`.

**Proven 2026-11-25:**

- 8 threads against fresh module state -> **7/8 raise the exact server error**, 1 succeeds.
- Server repro: cold boot -> `POST /chat` -> `prompt_len=1487 -> tokens=338 -> session=default -> kv_state resolved` -> immediately the same TypeError, before the first token. 3/3 cycles.
- This is the ONLY defective site. The four sibling lazy inits in `slonet_kernels.py` (`_kernels_built`, `_fused_built`, `_fused_norm_res_built`, `_lm_head_built`) all assign the value FIRST, set the flag LAST, and their readers null-check — so this is a single-site defect, not a pattern.

**Why it matters beyond the error:** in the first-request-after-boot window this aborts generation during prefill, so the request never reaches decode — it MASKS the native heap corruption tracked in card `20261122_150759` / the `_pool_run` card. Clearing it is a prerequisite for reproducing that crash end-to-end.

**Scope:**

- Delete the second variable: use `_nb_kv_kernels is not None` as the ready-test. One source of truth removes the ordering hazard instead of merely relying on it being correct.
- Preserve failure-caching semantics: `(None, None)` is non-None, so a numba failure stays cached (no per-call rebuild).
- TDD: race test — barrier + 8 threads against reset module state, asserting zero TypeErrors and that the flag is never observable `True` while the value is `None`. Red today (7/8), green after the fix.
- Do NOT touch the four already-correct `slonet_kernels.py` sites.

**Not in scope:** making numba opt-in/opt-out; the `_pool_run` C race (separate card).

**Verify:** race test green x10 consecutive; `tests/core-py/test_quantized_matmul.py` unchanged and green; `scripts/run_affected.sh tests/core-py`.
title: quantization: _get_nb_kv_kernels publishes its ready flag before the value — first-request TypeError

description:
**Goal:** `matmul_int8.c:_pool_run()` drives ONE global `g_pool` with no reentrancy guard. Two threads dispatching GEMMs at once corrupt each other's `done_seq` / `next_slice` / `arg`. Two symptoms from one missing guard: a proven deadlock, and the early-return UAF that produces the observed `free(): invalid next size (normal)` / `corrupted unsorted chunks` abort at `matmul_int8_f32`'s epilogue frees.

**Root cause (proven 2026-11-25 on pristine base `40da425db`, zero repo edits — all harness code lives outside the checkout):**

- `_pool_run` (`matmul_int8.c:485`) resets `g_pool.done_seq = 0`, `next_slice = 0`, `arg` and bumps `job_seq` under the mutex, then waits `while (done_seq < nworkers) pthread_cond_wait(&g_pool.done_cv)`.
- `done_cv` is signalled ONLY on the exact transition `++done_seq == nworkers`. With two waiters and a reset in between, the single signal lands on the wrong waiter — the other sleeps forever.
- Early-return branch: if the signal does reach the first caller, it returns while workers still hold its `a` and write `a.C`, so `matmul_int8_f32` runs `free(B_rowsum); free(Aq); free(Acc); free(Ascale)` on live buffers → heap metadata corruption → glibc abort. Statically shown; not yet caught dynamically (lost-wakeup dominates ~11:1).

**Evidence:**

- Control, 1 thread x3 -> 3/3 clean (a single dispatcher never fails — concurrency is the trigger).
- 4 threads x12 runs -> deadlock on run 1; ASan x8 -> deadlock x8; 2 threads x12 -> deadlock x11 + 1 pass; mixed-shape (1 long job + 3 hammers) x10 -> deadlock x1 + 9 pass.
- faulthandler stacks pinned at `wrapper.py:400 matmul_int8_f32_c` (the ctypes boundary) for every worker; all threads in `futex_do_wait` at 4.7% CPU for 5m45s over 600 matmuls.
- The four crash captures 2026-11-20/21 all end `Registered tool x10 -> lazy model materialized -> free() abort`.

**Why production reaches it:** `SloNetServer._model_lock` guards only `slonet_server.py:351/465`. The `slonet_provider.py` generate entry points (1645, 1735, 1836, 1983, 2060) take NO lock. On first request we also observed `parent-preload` spawning its own `SLNCParser` while the pump thread was still loading the model.

**Scope:**

- Add a `busy` flag published under `g_pool.mtx`. If already busy -> `unlock; return 0`, so `_gemm_run_threads`' existing per-call `pthread_create` fallback handles it (each worker gets its own `gemm_worker_arg` and is joined — no shared globals). Clear `busy` under the mutex after the wait, and in the `pid` fork-rebuild branch.
- TDD: port the stress harness into `tests/core-py/` — 4 threads, barrier, `join(timeout)` asserting none remain alive plus output finiteness. Red today, green after the guard.
- Gate: `scripts/run_affected.sh tests/core-py` plus `scripts/benchmark_slonet*.py`. The 1-thread control must stay clean and perf-neutral (this must not cost the common single-dispatcher path anything).

**Not in scope:** the `_get_nb_kv_kernels` publish race (separate card); `_block_j` / kernel arithmetic; the four already-correct `slonet_kernels.py` lazy inits.

**Verify:** 12/12 stress runs green under ASan with zero reports; 1-thread control unchanged; benchmark within noise of baseline.
title: quant_core: _pool_run has no reentrancy guard — concurrent GEMM dispatch deadlocks and UAFs in matmul_int8_f32

User go 2026-11-25 (design accepted in session). Core principle: content-addressed identity + append-only lineage; git never touches weights.

DESIGN BRIEF
1. Version id = content hash of merged state dict (recipe style like blake2b256/tokens/v1). Append-only bases/<id>/, never overwritten in place — the git model without binaries in git.
2. base_model field becomes the parent pointer (currently a literal 'sloughgpt' constant at train_pipeline.py:3253):

3. lineage field becomes the actual chain: 'v1 <- merge(adapter X, eval ...)' / 'v1 <- FT-on-corpus-Z'. Artifact registry already reads .soul sidecars -> version graph shows with no new infra.
4. Git stays in lane: code/fixtures/manifests only. Optional tiny committed JSON index (id -> path, parent, recipe, eval result). checkpoints/ + data/ stay untracked.
5. Merge-back = promotion event like a commit: merge_weights() (exists in lora.py) + save as v2 + record step-4 eval numbers. model_card.py already models base_model=outcome.model — the promotion review surface.

description:
Title:   Cypress fail-suppression: every test failure reports green
Status:  todo
Tags:    testing, ci, cypress, e2e, quality, area:web
Sprint:  ci-quality
GitHub:  -

Found during card 20261123_073036 (e2e chat-inference hang) on branch fix/chat-render-loop, 2026-11-25.

## Symptom
Three deliberate controls (plain throw in cy.then, chai assertion failure, cy.get timeout) ALL report PASSING under the project's cypress config — exit 0, no error text anywhere in the run log.

## Proof
- cypress/e2e/failure-controls.cy.ts + logs/failure-controls{1,3}.log: 3/3 controls green with support file.
- Same spec with --config supportFile=false (logs/failure-controls2.log): 3/3 fail correctly, EXIT=1, real error messages.
- Bisect: supportFile=cypress/support/diag-handlers.ts (handlers only) -> all green (suppressed); supportFile=cypress/support/diag-imports.ts (api-mocks + visual-commands only) -> 3 failing (normal).
=> The three handlers in cypress/support/e2e.ts are the suppressor.

## Root cause (verified in Cypress 14.5.4 bundle, ~/.cache/Cypress/14.5.4/.../cypress_runner.js)
cy.fail() does:  rets = Cypress.action('cy:fail', err, runnable)   // -> emitMap('fail', ...)
  if (rets && rets.length) return      // BAIL: failure swallowed
  return finish(err)                   // throw -> mocha fails the test
emitMap = map(listeners => lodash.map(listeners, listener))  // returns ONE entry PER LISTENER,
including listeners whose return value is undefined.
So merely REGISTERING a 'fail' listener makes rets non-empty -> every failure is swallowed,
regardless of the handler returning false or undefined. The handler's ternary
(isReactCommitCorruption(err) ? false : undefined) never matters: undefined still lands in rets.

## Impact
- Every e2e assertion failure in this repo is invisible; only run-level hangs/timeouts (exit 124) surface.
- chat-inference.cy.ts '3/3 green' is vacuous: the app is dead (rootChildren 0) and the 20s cy.get timeout is swallowed (evidence: cypress/evidence/aftereach.json, progress.json, logs/alive*.log).
- Any prior 'green' cypress gate on this harness is untrustworthy until fixed.

## Fix direction (NOT implemented — user ruling 2026-11-25: card only, separate fix)
- Do not blanket-register Cypress.on('fail'). Options: (a) drop the fail handler and keep only uncaught:exception suppression for React commit corruption (verify uncaught pipeline has the same emitMap shape first — it may NOT: uncaught:exception default path is different); (b) gate registration: register fail handler only when the error actually matches — impossible, registration is global at load; so (a) is the likely shape, plus a control spec (failure-controls.cy.ts) promoted to a permanent gate asserting that a deliberate failure FAILS.
- Keep isReactCommitCorruption suppression for the React 19.3 dev-build commit-corruption crash (card 9db3a320) — but via a path that does not blanket-swallow.

## Evidence index (worktree e2e-chat-hang, apps/web/cypress/)
- e2e/failure-controls.cy.ts, e2e/alive-probe.cy.ts
- support/diag-handlers.ts, support/diag-imports.ts (bisection support files)
- evidence/logs/failure-controls{1,2,3}.log, diag-handlers.log, diag-imports.log, alive{1..4}.log
- evidence/aftereach.json (swallowed 20s timeout recorded), progress.json, postvisit.json
title: Cypress fail-suppression: support/e2e.ts Cypress.on('fail') handler makes EVERY test failure report green (emitMap rets.length swallow)
